## Callidyrr dragoons

The Callidyrr dragoons were elite guards and knights in service to the High Kings of Callidyrr on the Moonshae Isles during the 15 century DR. To receive the title of "dragoon" was to be acknowledged for exceptional service to the crown.

Activities
Dragoons were members of the High King's guard and dedicated defenders of the realm, often hailed as champions of all Alaron. They were not part of Callidyrr's army (as were ordinary knights of the realm), but instead were sent in small numbers on special missions. Their tasks sometimes involved subterfuge, and so dragoons received special instruction in espionage and diplomacy. They were said to train equally in the skills of violent and nonviolent conflict resolution.

Callidyrr dragoons had the great honor of being able to speak with the authority of the High King, both figuratively and magically. They thus held great authority throughout Callidyrr, and furthermore had direct access to their monarch at the Palace of the High King in Caer Callidyrr. Needless to say, dragoons were expected to operate in good faith and with unwavering loyalty to the High King in exchange for the great privileges that they enjoyed. All dragoons vowed to serve their king and country, and took an oath administered by the Royal Hierophant, which bound them via a geas to the honored ancestors of Callidyrr. Violating this oath caused the fallen dragoon to permanently lose their memories.

Abilities
In addition to their training in diplomacy and physical fitness, dragoons were proficient with martial weapons and in mounted combat. They were also renowned for their tactical acumen and their familiarity with combat stratagems, with some developing an uncanny ability to predict and disrupt the movements of their melee opponents.

The words of a dragoon were infused with spiritual power by the noble Ffolk ancestors of Callidyrr, which caused their every verbal declaration to carry the weight of a royal decree or guarantee. Naturally, this led them to command respect from any who heard them, and made the dragoons highly influential, persuasive, and intimidating. In some cases, their voices allowed them to bestow power or comfort to their allies. The vows of more experienced dragoons could also be used to forge primal connections with others that allowed the dragoon to protect them, a power known as dragoon warding.

The mightiest dragoons were recognized by the Ffolk ancestors themselves as true knights of Callidyrr, and so would come to their aid if summoned. Such a dragoon summons was conducted by the dragoon focusing their will and letting out a traditional battlecry, which caused the arrival of a ghostly ancestral defender.

History
The first knights to be recognized as "dragoons" received this honor from High Queen Alicia Kendrick in the, when forces from Amn occupied Westphal and all efforts to dislodge them had failed. These dragoons were tasked with clandestinely battling the invaders, but subsequently became instrumental in putting down insurrections backed by loyalists of Lionel Carrathal after High Queen Kendrick died mysteriously (and was believed to have been poisoned) in the .Canon sources do not explicitly identify the insurgents during this event, but Brian R. James clarified in a Tweet that they were "Carrathal loyalists".

Despite failing to defeat the Amnians or to protect their queen, the dragoons earned a proud and valorous reputation throughout the following decades. Notably, they repelled sahuagin invasions, thwarted multiple assassination attempts, and defended the realm from the likes of giants and lycanthropes. They were also instrumental in brokering the tenuous peace between Callidyrr and the fey of Sarifal, which held through the late 15 century DR.

Members
To be named as a dragoon was to become a knight of Callidyrr (if the honoree was not one already). Dragoons were expected to be disciplined athletes, learned diplomats, and selfless protectors of both the realm and their allies alike. While dragoons were known to have a wide variety of skills, most were mighty close-quarters or mounted combatants, and generally had been fighters, paladins, or wardens prior to becoming dragoons. Higher ranks within the organization were awarded to those who had attained great respect among their allies, whether because of their experience or their extensive training.

Most dragoons were Ffolk humans or halflings, if for no other reason than Callidyrr's population was mostly human and halfling. While it was not inconceivable for heroes of other heritages to become a Callidyrr dragoon, anyone with strong fey ancestry was not welcome within their ranks, owing to the longstanding animosity between Callidyrr and the fey of Gwynneth.

## Camazotz

Camazotz was a chaotic evil lesser deity of bats from the Aztec or Central American pantheon who was worshiped on Toril by the beast cults and on Oerth as part of the Olman pantheon at the city of Tamoachan. On Oerth he was also venerated as a neutral evil lesser deity of vampires and the underworld, under the name Zotzilaha.

Description
Camazotz manifested as an enormous bat, and was never sighted without a thousand natural bats flocking about him.

An aspect of Zotzilaha took the form of a humanoid creature with the head and membranous wings of a monstrous bat, covered in coal-black fur. It had sharp fangs and wickedly hooked claws. Its eyes glowed orange and its body bore an aura of great heat.

Activities
If summoned, Camazotz might come if given an offering of countless insects for himself and his bat followers to feed on. This could be achieved with an insect plague spell. As Zotzilaha, he would often send his aspect to his shrines as a demonstration of his might and wrath.

Abilities
Camazoz was capable of the psionic power id insinuation.

An aspect of Zotzilaha could see clearly in any kind of darkness, even magical deeper darkness, and could speak with all bats and bat-like creatures. It could summon up to a dozen dire bats once a day. One infused with volcanic heat could breath a gout of unholy flame, burn those it clawed and those who touched it. It was immune to fire, as well as to paralysis, poison, and sonic energy, but vulnerable to cold. It could also summon fire bats instead.

Combat
Camazotz fought with his claws and fangs, and both inflicted a paralyzing venom. No weapon would harm him while he was in darkness.

Similarly, an aspect of Zotzilaha inflicted feverish tremors on those it harmed with its claws or bite. Its long arms gave it shocking long reach in battle.

Worshipers

Camazotz was revered by followers of the Cults of the Beast. His clerics were human and non-human, male and female, who typically wore leather helms and armor by way of raiment. Their holy days were nights of the quarter moon and venerated Camazotz with caves. The god's favored weapon was the javelin and a weapon of the deity spell would conjure a +1 distance javelin.

He was also venerated by assassins.

Appendix
Background
Camazotz, meaning "death bat" in the K'iche' language, is a figure in Mayan mythology. He was first adapted to D&D in Deities & Demigods 1st edition and the adventure module The Hidden Shrine of Tamoachan and its various adaptations for the Greyhawk setting and was later prominent in Dungeon magazine's Savage Tide adventure path. For the Forgotten Realms, Camazotz was only mentioned in Ed Greenwood's "Down-to-earth divinity" article in Dragon #54. While Camazotz/Zotzilaha has more lore and presence in Greyhawk, this article only covers general and Forgotten Realms–specific information, bar an overview of the Oerthian version in the lead. Please see the Great Library of Greyhawk wiki for more information.

## Catfish

Catfish, also called navalar in the Common tongue or barbjaws, were a carnivorous variety of game fish. They were among the most commonly eaten fish in Faerûn.

Description
Catfish generally had grayish-brown scales and delicate, pink flesh. They varied in size from very diminutive to huge, and were characterized by their barbels (also called "whiskers"), which were spiny, tentacle-like feelers around the corners of their mouths. In some cases, these whiskers secreted poisons of varying toxicity.

Some catfish could cross short patches of dry land. Other varietals of catfish were electric and could deliver powerful shocks to stun or kill both prey and predator. Scholars were unsure whether the source of this electric shock was mundane or magical.

Species
Drusk
A species of slow, brown-colored, flat-head catfish found throughout Faerûn and which were known for being good to eat. Although the name "drusk" was used in Amn and was widespread throughout the Realms thanks to being used by traders, local names differed: for example, they were known as "sarl" in Cormyr, the Dalelands, and Sembia and as "amaulings" or "amaul" in the coastal rivers of Tethyr.

Giant Catfish
Some mutant catfish could grow so large as to be called giant catfish. These usually could only be found in very large freshwater rivers and lakes and tended to be aggressive toward anything that might fit inside their mouths.

Irrinda

A common electric catfish found within the shallow rivers of the northern Chultan peninsula. Despite its diminutive size, it was capable of discharging a shock that would paralyze or kill the smaller fish on which it preyed.

Likoto

Another common electric catfish found in the rivers of Chult, the likoto was a scavenger that was equally at home in slow or fast-moving waters. They were small and had the unusual habit of swimming upside-down in order to better feed on the bottom of floating debris, such as fallen logs.

Minjiriya

A large species of electric catfish found within the riverways of the northern Chultan peninsula, the minjiriya was able to discharge an electric shock powerful enough to kill an adult human. Chultan fishers were suitably wary of them.

Spiny Sleeper
The spiny sleeper was a toxic cousin to the catfish that could be found in the Great Glacier.

Stalking Catfish
The stalking catfish was a cousin to the giant catfish that could be found within the Underdark, and which could survive outside of water for a considerable time.

Verme
Another cousin to the giant catfish, verme were large carnivorous predators characterized by their large scales and needle-like teeth. They could be found in the tropical and subtropical waters of Kara-Tur.

Ecology
Many types of catfish were found throughout freshwater lakes and riverbeds in temperate, warm, subtropical, and tropical environments. Blind varietals could also be found in underground waters.

Catfish were primarily scavengers and bottom-feeders, and were not picky in what they attempted to eat. Some also hunted and fed on smaller species of fish, which occasionally made them competition for communities who also ate those same fish.

They were a favorite food of catoblepas and crocodiles.

Habitats
Catfish could be found from the temperate, subtropical, and tropical freshwaters of Kara-Tur (notably in the Dreaming River on the Malatran Plateau) and the Chultan peninsula (notably in the River Soshenstar and in Lake Grunglung) to the much colder waters of northern Faerûn, such as the streams and rivers of Amn (notably in the Alandor River), Cormanthor (notably in the Elvenflow but also in the Deeping and Semberflow), Cormyr and Sembia (notably in the Starwater River), the Dalelands (notably in the Dalestream), the Dessarin Valley (notably in the River Dessarin itself, but also the Laughingflow and the River Surbrin), the Moonshae Isles, and the Western Heartlands (notably in the River Chionthar), as well as in Highstar Lake of the High Moor and the great lake of the Moonsea. They could occasionally be found in saltwater environments, such as the Sea of Fallen Stars.

Catfish could be found in the shallow streams branching off of the River Styx on the plane of Pandemonium, and such specimens could grow to surprising size.

Uses

A plump catfish could provide a good meal for two adults. They were widely eaten in Faerûn, most notably in places like the Sword Coast, the Heartlands, the Lake of Steam, the Lands of Intrigue, and the North; in the Underdark; in Kara-Tur, most notably in Wa and Malatra; and in Zakhara. Nixies kept herds of catfish as food, alongside the likes of bass and trout. Dwarven citadels were said to sometimes maintain cisterns where they raised blind catfish and trout meant to serve as food in case of a siege. They were also kept by the grung of Chult.

As a game fish, they were recreationally fished in places like Cormanthor, the Moonshaes and Port Nyanzaru. Centaurs maintained catfish ponds that they were careful not to deplete.

Whether for food or for sport, anglers sought to catch catfish with bait ranging from leatherjackets and nightcrawlers to moldy cheese and pieces of fat. Some Faerûnian fishers had a method for hunting catfish that involved reaching one's hand directly into a suspected den. This method was not only discouraged but mocked by fishers in places like Chult, where electric catfish like the minjiriya could kill someone who attempted it.

Availability
 The Copper Coronet in Athkatla included catfish guts in its popular and affordable "sark" stew.
 In Crimmor, a common "sward-feast" (i.e., picnic food) was throus, which featured smoked drusk catfish.
 The Laughing Goblin Inn in Phlan served blackened catfish from the Moonsea.
 The Painted Boat in Ravens Bluff served freshcaught river catfish.
 The Scaly Catfish was an inn and tavern in Nagarr that served poorly cooked fish.
 In Waterdeep, a dish called melverfew was made by slowly cooking diced eels, mushrooms, catfish, and flounder in oxen-and-onion gravy.
 The Wemic Comes to Westbridge was a restaurant in Westbridge that served spiced catfish topped with parsley cream.
 In Yartar, the Fishyard market was known for its fresh daily catches of catfish and other river fish.

History
The dwarven city of Iltkazar, built during the height of Shanatar, maintained drainage pits in which catfish were raised as a food source.

During the height of the elven empire of Cormanthyr, catfish was considered a feasting food and a delicacy in some circles.

Catfish were eaten in ancient Netheril, and could be purchased from fishmongers at Low Netherese markets like those in Dalekeva. Prior to the creation of the Anauroch desert, they could be found in Netheril's Moray River.

In Wa, a magic stream on the Fochu Peninsula was known as the Catfish Stream. Anyone who leapt into the stream while holding a sack filled with a handful of blue mahogany dust had a chance of a catfish manifesting within the sack. In some cases, a message might be visible on catfish's scales, while in some other cases, the scales might instead be poisonous to the touch.

By the mid-to-late 14 century DR, poor villagers in places like Bogbrook in Cormyr and Uthmere in the Great Dale caught their own catfish, making it an important source of food. In urban restaurants in the Realms, fresh catfish could be ordered for 5 copper pieces, meaning it was one of the more affordable fish.

In the late 15 century DR, the Red Wizard Imaraska made use of illusory flying catfish to scout and patrol for her.

## Catatonia

Catatonia was a condition characterized by a complete withdrawal from reality.

Acquisition
Catatonia could appear as a response to a terrible shock or horror, long-term mistreatment, or a magical mental attack. The mind defended itself from this external peril by closing itself off entirely. This could last only a short time or be practically indefinite.

Symbol of sleep sent its victims into a catatonic sleep, which they could not be woken from.

Effects
A catatonic person was unable to interact with the world, as their mind refused to receive stimuli. They would typically slump to the ground or stand completely still, unable to speak, move, or preserve themselves, even in cases of personal peril and injury. They wouldn't be able to eat or drink on their own, and in some cases couldn't even do that with assistance. They might be able to be led around with guidance and even directed to perform simple tasks, but this would end without direct supervision.

When sufficiently agitated, it was possible for a catatonic person to have a sudden outburst of violence against the source of irritation. This would only last a short time before they fell back into an insensible state.

A catatonic person had such strong unconscious mental defenses that their mind was effectively protected by both mind blank and tower of iron will. This made telepathic communication (or further mental injuries) extremely difficult or impossible.

Notable Affected
 The father of Catlindra Serpentar became catatonic after seeing his daughter slay a doppelganger in the form of her mother.
 Droth, a Howling Hatred cultist taken prisoner by the rival Black Earth cult.
 Imoen went into a state of catatonia after her soul was removed in Spellhold by Jon Irenicus and Bodhi.
 Keletheryl, an elf trapped in Nalavara's hoard demiplane, became increasingly consumed by guilt and remorse, and regularly fell into a catatonic state as he looked inward.
 Zan, a child, entered a catatonic state after being magically interrogated by Elden Vargas and the Ashmadai. He was only able to mumble warnings about the cult.

## Call weaponry

Call weaponry was a psionic power of the psychoportation discipline and its teleportation subdiscipline that manifested a weapon into the hands of the psionics user.

Effects
Though to the eyes it appeared to manifest something out of thin air, call weaponry actually teleported a random simple, martial, or exotic weapon from elsewhere in the multiverse, or even from another time period, into the waiting hands of the manifester. The manifester could not call upon a specific weapon, only a broad kind, such as a longsword, a warhammer, etc. If they called upon a ranged weapon, such as a crossbow or sling, the weapon would be accompanied by 3 to 18 appropriate, non-magical projectiles. All weapons summoned by the power were made of common materials, were considered magic weapons, and emitted a low hum.

Once summoned, a weapon remained for a period of one or more hours, but would prematurely disappear back from whence it came if the manifester relinquished their grip on it fore more than 12 seconds. Additionally, a manifester could focus their reserve of psychic energy into further augmenting the weapon summoned by call weaponry, granting them +1 or greater enchantment bonuses.

Older versions of the power relied more upon the manifester's skills in psionics to determine what kind of weapons they could manifest, with greater skill corresponding to greater weaponry, but also greater costs of psychic energy.

Display
This power exhibited an auditory and material display.

Users
This power was knowable by psionicists and psychic warriors, as well as ardents and divine minds that followed the justice mantle.

Known/Notable Users
 Teliene Coloara, a drow illithid slayer and psychic warrior.

## Cancer

Cancer was an invariably deadly non-magical disease that was present on Toril.

Treatment
Cancers that were not understood as such were often mistaken for curses, and so were treated with arcane spells. Some especially virulent, supernatural cancers could only be treated with spells such as limited wish and wish.

Acquisition
The Color Spray Nebula in Realmspace cured all other diseases, but had a small yet statistically significant chance of inducing an especially persistent cancer, one immune to all magical cures.

Elven metabolism was less susceptible to cancer, though half-drow were strongly susceptible to a particular form of skin cancer due to sunlight exposure.

History
Essemra Ruldegost died of a sickness that would most likely have had a cancer diagnosis had she been diagnosed elsewhere.

Cancer was a point of comparison for many virulent afflictions, and was named in the tale of the Earthmother in the Moonshaes.

## Castle Iron Guard

Castle Iron Guard was the largest castle in the city of Ravens Bluff and one of its two primary troop garrisons in the 14 century DR. During the Three Women War, the fortress acted as a base of operations for the City Defense Forces.

Location
This castle was located on the northeastern hills of the city, overlooking the Fire River and across from the Central Cemetery.

Description
Castle Iron Guard was built atop an ancient dwarven keep, which was repurposed as a vast underground storage space. The fortress also had one of the largest stables in Ravens Bluff, including one pen that was meant to act as a backup stable for the Griffon Guard's griffons.

Inhabitants
Castle Iron Guard garrisoned more than one third of Ravens Bluff's military, as well as a considerable number of priests and wizards. This included the High Sorcerer, commander of the Guardians of the Celestial Mysteries, and the army chaplain core's High Patriarch. The fortress also acted as the secret headquarters of a clandestine organization known only as the Brotherhood.

Beyond combatants, the fortress housed a large number of workmen, tradesmen, and livestock to keep it operational.

History
Around the, in the early days of the Three Women War, the Ravens Bluff Army put out a call to mercenaries in the Ravens Bluff Trumpeter, telling them to report to Castle Iron Guard for a contract and assignment.

Late into the war, the Ravens Bluff Army caught win of the enemy planning an attack on Mossbridges and routed their forces there for battle. However, this was merely a ruse orchestrated by the turncoat Commander Nioga and his Company of the Bloody Hatchets, meant to draw the army away so that Myrkyssa Jelan's forces could invade the city without interference. A group of six adventurers in the army learned of Nioga's deceit and were sent home by General Obespieri to warn General Koran Therogeon, commander of the City Defense Forces.

They rode hard through the night to reach Ravens Bluff in time. When they arrived around dawn, the City Guardsmen informed them that Nioga had rode through earlier asking where he could find Therogeon. Sources differ on whether the adventurers managed to arrive to Castle Iron Guard in time to confront Nioga, but most agree that by the time they arrived they found Therogeon murdered at his desk.  Lady Caroline Skyhawk, Therogeon's second-in-command, would arrive shortly thereafter. Shocked at the gruesome scene, she demanded to be debriefed on the situation.

Quickly ascertaining the truthfulness of the adventurers' words, Skyhawk snapped to action and wasted no time in yelling out the door at office boy Tremai to "Quickly, rouse the commanders, the runners and the entire staff! We are under attack! Sound the warning bells, prepare the gates! And Tremai, get the High Sorcerer in here, in his small clothes if necessary!" Before long cries of "Attack" and "Awaken" rang throughout the fortress. She then turned to the adventurers, told them to get rest and report to her by next dawn, and began to intently study a map that had been spread across Therogeon's desk.

Relationships
Callia was the mother of the High Lady Ordalf, the founder and Queen of Sarifal. By the end of Callia's life, her daughter hated her, and thought of her as a "whore" for having fallen in love and borne a child with a non-leShay. That child was Amaranth, whose father was a simple and upstanding Llewyrr elf, a Knight of Synnoria, and brother of Lord Mindarion of Synnoria.

Because of the intense importance placed on the "purity" of the leShay bloodline, Ordalf's son (and Callia's grandson), Prince Araithe, had desired to sire a child with Callia. However, she rebuffed him.

History
Callia was many thousands of years old by the time of her death in the 15 century DR. Her elder daughter, Ordalf, was at least eleven millennia old at the time.

Following the death of Ordalf's father—ostensibly from venereal disease—Callia had a child with a Llewyrr elf in the late 1450s DR. By this time, she had already spurned her grandson Ariathe's advances, and when he discovered that she had a child with an elf, he had both her and her lover hunted down and killed in his jealous rage. He subsequently brought their seven-year-old daughter, Amaranth, to his base at Citadel Umbra with the intention of grooming his young aunt to become a future mother of his children.

Prior to her death, Callia was promised by one of Amaranth's caretakers, Valeanne, to protect the girl if anything happened to her.

## Cauldron of gateways

A cauldron of gateways was a rare enchanted cauldron that had the power to create gates to any destination on the same plane of existence, but also acted adequately as a regular cooking pot.

Powers
In order to activate this cauldron, a user had to bring fresh water to a steaming boil, then put in some soil from the desired destination, and finally utter the command words "I demand a path". Once all steps were carried out, a translucent image of the location where the soil originated would manifest in the steam arising from the cauldron. The steam acted as a gate, with stepping through it transporting individuals to the depicted location. The steam would stay active for around twenty minutes to as long as two bells. If stepping through the steam as it was deactivating, there was a chance an individual's body could be bisected.

A cauldron of gateways could be used once per week and was unable to be transported through its own gate.

Appendix
See Also
Cauldron of planar travel

## Cauldron of planar travel

A cauldron of planar travel was a rare and massive enchanted cauldron that had the power to create portals.

Powers
These cauldrons functioned almost identically to a cauldron of gateways. The steps to activating it included bringing fresh water to a steaming boil inside of it, then put in some soil from the desired destination, and finally uttering the command words "I demand a path". Once all steps were carried out a translucent image of the location where the soil originated would manifest in in the steam arising from the cauldron, with he steam acting as a portal. The steam would remain active for around twenty minutes to as long as two bells.

This effect could only be activated once per week. The cauldron was unable to be transported through its own portal. And if an individual were to step through the steam as it was deactivating, there was a chance their body could be bisected.

Where it differed from a cauldron of gateways was in it not being limited to opening portals to locations on the same plane of existence. A cauldron of planar travel could open portals to any plane in the multiverse, so long as soil from the desired plane of existence was placed inside.

## Castle of Sorcery

The Castle of Sorcery was the residence of the mage Ilhundyl until the .

Location
The castle was in the Calishar.

Interior
The location included at least one room for meetings, with a throne room, and one that included a lectern and a crystal on which he conducted conversations with faraway individuals.

One of its rooms was called the Wind Cavern, which had a number of glass sculptures riddled with holes that made music of sorts when wind passed through them. The room had an archway leading to the northern tower of the castle, and this archway was flanked with suits of armor. This room was also close to the Great Gate of the castle.

Defenses
A maze outside the gates held numerous traps, both magical and mechanical, many of which were illusionary walls and invisible portals. There were hungry lions that could be released to hunt down intruders, as well as guardian golems and trapped statues that shot lightning out of their hands. Some of the pit traps had to be powered manually by men on wheels. There were also archers, and some golems that were joined with the walls.

The Wind cavern in particular had panels that could reveal death tyrants, a hidden cage full of winged serpents, and numerous glyphs.

History
Ilhundyl was banished from Volothamp in, and had almost certainly gained his castle by then.

He received a visit from the Mystran priestess Elmara, secretly prince Elminster Aumar of Athalantar, in, where she asked for his guidance in knowing magic; he bid her find Ondil's Book of Spells, which she acquired by, yielding it up at Mystra's Dance in the mouth of the Delimbiyr River, where he then stole it without her knowledge. The prince came back without his disguise in, attacking and slaying Ilhundyl with the help of the sorceress Myrjala Talithyn. Afterwards, she used spellfire to raze and torch much of the castle's insides.

Inhabitants
Ilhundyl had numerous servants, one in particular being Garadic, a shapeshifting creature of sorts, and another being a female lich of unknown provenance that was enslaved to his will in some way.

## Caer Corwell (castle)

Caer Corwell was a castle that had long been the seat of the Kendrick kings of Corwell on the island of Gwynneth in the Moonshae Isles. It overlooked the small city of Corwell, sometimes also known as "Caer Corwell" in honor of the castle. The castle was in ruins as of the late 15 century DR.

Location

The keep was located on a rocky cliff several hundred feet high that overlooked the common fields of Corwell and the waters of the harbor. This position made the keep visible from a great distance, and in particular, it could be seen from nearly a day's travel away along the Corwell Road.

Structure
The castle was surrounded by a high wooden palisade which ended in a stone gatehouse. The front gates of the castle were made of strong wood and an iron portcullis was lowered from the gatehouse, which had four stout watchtowers. Rising above the wide courtyard, the central keep was protected by three parapeted towers. Prior to the fall of the kingdom of Corwell, the banner of the Kendrick family (a silver bear on a black field) hung in splendor from the tallest point of the castle.

As of the late 15 century DR, the castle was a crumbling shell of its former self, and the roof had caved in.

Interior
Within the keep, Caer Corwell had a huge hall with two great oak tables and a large fireplace in the corner. Adjoining to this hall were the barracks, stables, and other outbuildings, all of which sat safely within the outer palisade.

Defenses
While the wooden wall was a point of weakness, the position of the castle atop the steep, rocky hill balanced this by making it extremely dangerous for attackers to even approach the wall. The only way to reach the gate was to climb the winding road up the hill, which was completely exposed to defensive arrows and burning oil from the castle.

The garrison was led by an exceptionally skilled fighter. Below him were 10 sergeants, each of whom commanded about twenty soldiers.

History
The sturdy castle had a long history as a proven redoubt in times of conflict, and was famed at the time of the Darkwalker War for having never fallen to an invader.

Corwell fell in the early 15 century DR when the fey of Sarifal expelled all humans from the island of Gwynneth. The Kendricks who still resided at the castle were killed.

As of the late 15 century DR, the ruins of the castle had come to be occupied by a mad gnome known as Phillwyp the Wary, alongside his boggart minions, who aspired to rule a kingdom of unseelie fey. During this time, High King Derid Kendrick of Callidyrr aspired to reclaim his family's ancestral seat.

## Caer Moray (castle)

Caer Moray was a castle on the island of Moray in the Moonshae Isles. It overlooked the small city of Moray, sometimes also known as "Caer Moray" in honor of the castle. The castle was in ruins as of the late 15 century DR.

Location
The castle lay on the northeastern side of the town. It sat atop a low hill with a rocky pinnacle standing above a rocky beach.

Structure
The main keep sat atop the pinnacle of rock above the beach, while the hilltop that controlled access to it was ringed by a stone curtain wall punctuated with five round towers and a variety of guard buildings. The walls in turn were surrounded by a moat, with a drawbridge allowing access to the  main gate. As of the late 15 century DR, all of these structures were in ruins: the wall had toppled and the drawbridge was gone, and instead a causeway of rubble had been created to serve as a bridge.

Interior
The courtyard leading up to the keep was full of stone cisterns plus a well that could be used to access a sea cave beneath the ruined keep. Even after the fall of the castle, the multistory keep remained intact enough that the banquet hall and upper floors were mostly usable, and occasionally a storage room might be found that had remained remarkably pristine.

Defenses
Naphthalene could be poured and ignited upon attackers from hidden cisterns within the old walls. When those walls still stood, the wooden main gate was the weakest point in the defenses.

History
As of the, the capital of Moray lacked a castle, a clear sign of how poor the Kingdom of Moray was at the time. It was the only Ffolk realm without such a fortress, and residents were forced to flee to defensive towers away from the coast if they came under attack from Northlander raiders. Caer Moray was constructed in the following decades, and had been completed by the time of the Spellplague in the, only to fall shortly afterward. It came under attack by lycanthropes of the Black Blood tribe, who tore down its walls.

The castle was subsequently reclaimed following the arrival on Moray of Lady Amaranth, a leShay princess from Sarifal who came to lead a group of mostly female and good lycanthropes out of the ruins beginning in the late 1460s DR. Within a decade, they had largely rebuilt the defensive walls, and had adapted the keep's banquet chamber into a place where they could craft metal goods and textiles. They soon became a beacon of protection for the humans who had settled the northern coast of Moray in the years since the lycanthrope attacks, and were known to celebrate a version of the Feast of Stags in which they freely shared food during hard winter months.

These lycanthropes were seen as heretics by the Black Blood tribe, and when Malar was revived on Moray in the late 1470s DR, they launched an assault on the castle in the Battle of Caer Moray. They scaled the walls and battered down the gate, and it was only thanks to the intervention of Chauntea that the defenders were saved: the godess sent a massive wave to sweep away the attackers. However, it was also Chauntea's will that Lady Amaranth leave Moray, and so her wave also toppled the newly rebuilt walls, thus largely ending the community that had been established there. Amaranth departed, leaving the survivors in the hands of her adopted sisters, Lightfoot and Bay.

## Cashew soup

Cashew soup was a thick, nut-based soup in the Realms whose primary seasoning was its namesake ingredient, cashew nuts.

History
In the, when Tennora Hedare's Aunt Aowena and Uncle Eckhart came to visit her home in Waterdeep's Castle Ward, a tenement building called the God Catcher, she spent most of the morning preparing a pot of cashew soup for them. This was accompanied by morsels of bread and salty ham, which took Tennora an hour to assemble and were largely made so that her aunt wouldn't notice that she was out of butter. However, Aunt Aowena was so displeased with the local conditions compared to their home back in the North Ward that she barely touched her bowl of soup.

## Cambridge

The Cambridge family were a Ffolk royal line in the Moonshae Isles.Canon sources do not identify where the Cambridge family ruled in the Moonshae Isles, although it is implied in the Black Wizards novel (ch. 21) that the family name was in use on the isle of Gwynneth.

History
Like all royal families of the Moonshaes, the Cambridges traced their lineage to the Cymrych family of High Kings and Queens. However, following the decline of the Cymrych dynasty in the 10 century DR, the Cambridges allowed the spelling and pronunciation of their name to change in order to better differentiate themselves from other Cymrych families.

The Cambridges remained a recognizable royal name as of the mid–14 century DR, alongside the Kendricks of Corwell, the Kimballs of Moray, and the Kincaids of Snowdown.

## Cabal

Cabals were informal organizations all across the Realms. They usually formed in a very local area.

They consisted of informal alliances between persons, merchant families, or just peddlers, or any variation of such, who manipulated trade on a very small local scale in their favor. They engaged in nepotism (a cabal member's incompetent relative would be hired by another cabal member, where possible), trade redirection (if a buyer was looking for a trade good and a member of a cabal heard this, the buyer would be directed to a member of that cabal who dealt in that good), price-fixing, vacant land buying, and other underhanded, but mostly harmless actions. Elminster believed some of these cabals to even be benevolent.

Some cabals tended to be more aggressive, driving away any foreign merchant that dared to settle in their area of influence by hiring bandits to attack them or rob them and, in extreme cases, destroying that merchant's property or burning the foreigner's trade houses.

## Calimport/Hook Ward

The Hook Ward was one of the four Port Wards of Calimport, making up the eastern third of the city's public docks.

Description
Whilst the upper classes of Calimshan rarely made much in the way distinguishing between the Port Wards, the Hook Ward stood out among its peers as being a balanced blend between the commercial and the militant. Its streets were far cleaner and more organized than those of the Dock Ward. It was also the site of the actual shipyards that serviced the city's port and many of the city's seafarers' guilds had their guildhalls based here.

One of the other aspects of Hook Ward that made it stand out amongst the other Port Wards was the predominance of temples and shrines to maritime deities, both major and minor. Very few of these religious sites stood out as particularly luxuriant compared to the temples of the Upper Muzad. Many temples of other wards commonly sent proselytes and new acolytes down into the Hook Ward's markets and dock areas to perform streetside sermons, hoping to draw the attention of new arrivals to their own god and house of worship, but more often than not this would culminate in proselytes of opposing churches duking it out on the streets.

Government
In the 14 century DR, the second son of Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal, Tahyr yn Ralan el Pesarkhal, was the Sultan of Hook Ward. A rather apolitical and hardworking seafarer, the Sultan of Hook Ward was also the ralbahr of the Nallojal, Calimshan's navy, and the sabbalad of the Eraré Sabban. He typically spent about two months of the year out at sea, during which time his brother-in-law and Syl-Vizar of the Hook Ward, Khomaya, would take over as acting sabbalad.

As for the Syl-Pasha, he notably visited the Hook Ward and its Eraré Sabban more than any other sabban outside of the Palace
and Grand Wards. He could invariably be found presenting himself every time a new dignitary or emissary of noble birth showed up to one of the embassies in the Eraré Sabban.

In a way the Hook Ward held undue control over the flow of entry into the city of Calimport, for no more than five people could exit from a docked ship until its docking fees were cleared with the harbormasters.

Defenses
The ward had a more subdued military presence compared to the Armada Ward.

Of its three sabbans, Eraré was afforded additional security in the 14 century DR, due to being a core component of Syl-Pasha Ralan's long-term plans to grow the nation's foreign trade. The Ajvent Sabban and Osiir Sabban were afforded two amlakkhans and a sadidah. By contrast, the Eraré Sabban was afforded two sadidah, three amlakkhans, two minarets dedicated to its defenses, and an additional garrison of troops that were assigned to its embassies.

Visting foreign officials usually brought their own guards and servants, though the local Mercenaries' Guild insisted that to ensure safety an embassy should have no less than 25 guards on duty. Because of this, the guild would provide their own warriors to fill out the ranks.

Trade
Much like in other parts of the port city, one could find all manner of things for sale within the bazaars of the Hook Ward.

Sabbans
The Hook Ward was divided into three sabbans with nine drudachs.
Ajvent Sabban
Also known as the "Shipwrights' Sabban" or the "Sails Sabban", this sabban comprised the entirety of Calimport's shipyards. It was adjacent to the Caravans Ward's Drakhon Sabban and the Maker's Ward's Golnar Sabban. It was under the shared control of Sultan Tahyr, the Sabbalad Saibh el Daafib, and the pasha of shipwrights. The underlings of the sultan handled the day-to-day operations of the sabban, making sure the ruler's ships had highest priority, including in terms of maintenance or repairs. Not even visiting ships from Calimshan's allies would receive precedence over the Sultan's vessels.

The sabban mark of Ajvent depicted a leaping dolphin above a curling wave. It was divided into three drudachs—Amra Drudach, Calik Drudach, and Ninar Drudach.
Notable Locations
Algharabadah The three-story guildhall of the Packers Guild.Location: Amra Drudach
Ghaebir's Villas Two fancy houses belonging to the Pasha Ghaebir, one standing three stories tall and the other four stories.Location: Ninar Drudach
Hook Sadidah A fancy, three-story barracks of the sabban's sadimmin.Location: Ninar Drudach
Nichtwahradh One of the many luxurious homes of the Sultan of Hook Ward. Rumors had it that Tahyr had around sixteen personal homes across the ward, all of which he rented or loans out to his close friends, trade allies, and other individuals.Location: Calik Drudach
Semasim Villas Two fancy houses belonging to the Pasha Semasim, one standing three stories tall and the other four stories.Location: Ninar Drudach
Houses of Walaf Two houses belonging to Walaf, the druzir of the Calik Drudach in the 14 century DR. One was more opulent, standing four stories tall, whilst the other was one of the three-story tall mud-brick row houses that made up a large portion of Calimport's buildings.Location: Calik Drudach

Eraré Sabban
Also known as the "Wyvern Sabban" or more commonly the "Wraith Sabban", Eraré was the central sabban of the Hook Ward. It served as the receiving for dignitaries, a space for many of the embassies of foreign powers, and was frequently an unofficial meeting place among adventurers. It was also notably the most safest place in all of the Port Wards, due to its high security. Its latter moniker was derived from a horrid creature known as the "Eraré Wraith".

The sabban mark of Eraré was originally a warhammer, backed by a silhouette of a wyvern in flight. Over time the warhammer disappeared from the sigil, though it could still be found on some of the ward's walls. The sabban was divided into three drudachs—Badjit Drudach, Taorahl Drudach, and Tynar's Drudach. They were each defined by the particular services that they offered the sabban, which helped the Amlakkar to maintain order by isolating pockets of trouble.
Badjit Drudach
Located directly on the waterfront, the Badjit Drudach was Eraré's drudach of entertainment, being home to the majority of the sabban's festhalls and taverns.
Notable Locations
Amlakkhan Badjit One of the ward's three guard barracks, it was a building that stood three-stories tall.
The Everful Jacket The guildhall of the Entertaining Society of Taverners and a tavern.
Festhall of Eternal Delight A major temple dedicated to Sharess. It alone contributed to the Badjit Drudach being the most renowned drudach in all of the Hook Ward.
House of the Silken Pillows A rather standard, three-story inn of the mud brick rowhouse variety.
House of Sabira el Wijada The private residence of Sabira el Wijada.
Muham's Inn A rather standard, four-story inn of the mud brick rowhouse variety.
R'taalin Armorers An armorer's store.
The Rolling Waves A moderately fancy three-story inn.
The Seven Dancing Jhasinas An opulent festhall whose employees were adherents of Sharess.
Sune's Abandon A moderately fancy three-story festhall.
Vaoladah Khanduq A delapidated khanduq that acted as a central gathering point and watering hole amidst the Badjit Drudach's bazaar.
The Veiled Dance A rather standard, two-story festhall of the mud brick rowhouse variety.
The Wraithshaven A rather standard, four-story inn of the mud brick rowhouse variety.

Taorahl Drudach
Also known as the "Twelvetors Drudach", the Taorahl Drudach was dedicated to providing the service of lodgings. It was the easternmost drudach, nestled against the shipyard walls of Hook Ward and the Wizard Ward. It was home to the residences of the sabban's leaders, most of the lodgings that were available to the sabban's visitors, and in 1370 DR was selected by the Syl-Pasha as the site for foreign embassies meant to further gain foreign alliances in commerce and politics. The "Twelvetors" nickname was derived from the presence of twelve minarets in the Taorahl skyline. Three of these belonged to amlakkhans, six were attached to opulent villas, and three belonged to temples.

The embassies of the Taorahl Drudach provided free living space for visiting dignitaries and officials of foreign powers, but more specifically they each possessed living quarters for no less than three dignataries and their families. They were all beautiful houses and villas, standing three stories tall, with offices, meeting rooms, kitchens, pantries, basement quarters for servants (or slaves), and a grand hall for parties. They stood apart from one another through distinct stylistic and structural differences.

Early on, none of the embassies were used as permanent residences for ambassadors and their support staff, though there were hopes that such a thing could be established by 1371 DR as Calimshan developed more binding relations with foreign powers. In particular, sights were set on this occuring with the Cormyreans and Thayvians, whose trade delegates were visiting Calimport with greater frequency each month in 1370 DR.

When the embassies were first established, they were met with a mixed reception from the Taorahl Drudach's many pashas. Whilst some railed about it giving non-Calishites an undeserved social status above their own and desires to claim their housing, others viewed this as the opening of new business opportunities. Local pashas and businessmen would spend great sums in hopes of endearing themselves. And local businesses would supply most of the food and drink available at embassy meetings, having them brought over from nearby inns and taverns.

For those who resided within embassies, it was socially expected to sponsor a gala at the residence a night or two before one left Calimport. This gave both the visitors and local a chance to settle any final business then, as well as a final chance for the pashas and other social climbers in Calimport to either endear themselves or slander their political rivals.
Notable Locations
A Marid's Flagon A low class, two-story tall tavern.
Amlakkhan Taorahl One of the ward's three guard barracks, it was a building of the classic mud-brick variety and stood three-stories tall.
The Chawal's House A modest five-story tall rowhouse.
Chedlara's Kisses An inn.
Cormyrean Embassy A villa designated as the embassy of Cormyr. In its first year of operation, the building was resided in by Jhartos Illance and his elder cousin, Captain Mallik Illance.
The Eye Tyrant's End A low class, two-story tall tavern.
The Eye Tyrant's Khanduq A khanduq that was the heart of the Taorahl Drudach's central bazaar. Several shops and merchant tents could be found along its outer walls, forming temporary, narrow avenues. Among the great deal of businesses that resided within the khanduq were The Anvil of Twelve Eyes, Fadila's Slippers and Boots, Maajan Silvers, Ranil's Rugs and Tapestries, Said's Herbs and Unguents, Shields Italazar, The Yoxen's Yield Leathers, The Yuadarzah Scimitars, and Wanda's Silken Fineries.
Furlesahdah The guildhall of the Shipwrights' Guild.
El Ghaelidah A rather standard, two-story tavern of the mud brick variety.
Gharab's Jewels A jewelry business.
The Golden Haired Harpy A tavern owned by the company Golden Sands Brewery.
Green Wyvern Trade Company warehouse Newly built in 1370 DR, this white-washed warehouse belonged to the Green Wyvern Trade Company.
Jet Jambiya A popular neutral meeting ground and open-air courtyard enclosed by two-story bar whose building was G-shaped. Locals referring to "Jet Jambiya" meant the mystical jambiya that hovered in the air above its courtyard.
Khomaya Villa One of the larger villas of the whole Hook Ward, this opulent mansion and the equally massive khamarkha in its rear grounds were the private residence of Syl-Vizar Khomaya.
Kyel Villa A cluster of buildings hidden behind high walls, this compound was the private residence of Kyel, a pasha and one of the Druzir of the Taorahl Drudach. Considered one of the most paranoid among the pashas, Kyel rarely left his villa, only ever doing so under the company of at least a dozen bodyguards.
Melek's Fine Silks and Textiles A textiles shop.
Minaret of Baadilhaela An elegant, eight-sided and six-stories tall minaret belonging to Pasha Baadilhaela. It bore a near identical resemblance to a particular khamarkha tower in the city of Memnon.
The Oasis of the White Jonquil A rather standard, four-story inn of the mud brick rowhouse variety.
Sadidah Taorahl A garrison of the city guard, a three-story tall building of the mud-brick variety.
The Seldarinardah A mud-brick style rooming house that stood out amongst the rest for the elven artwork displayed on its facade.
Seven Draughts One of the most prosperous inns the Hook Ward in the 14 century DR, it was renowned for the safety its offered patrons.
The Scholar's Priory A walled temple complex dedicated to the allied deities Deneir, Milil, and Oghma.
Shou Embassy A villa designated as the embassy of Shou Lung.
The Silver Circles A modest two-stories tall inn.
Sultan's Palace The private residence of Sultan Tahyr, the most simplest of the three villas that he owed in the Eraré Sabban, and the on in which he chose to live in. It was directly attached to the villa of Sabbalad Khomaya.
Tabuq's Nightmares An upscale shop that dealt in obscure knowledge, dungeoneering intel, and trophies.
Thayvian Embassy A villa designated as the embassy of Thay.
Tomed's Locks and Chains A locksmith business on the ground floor of a four-story tall rowhouse of the mud-brick variety.
Veiled Glances A rather standard, three-story festhall of the mud brick rowhouse variety.
The Vihaddah Semohl A festhall and shrine dedicated to Iyachtu Xvim.

Tynar's Drudach
Also known by many as the "Three Temples Drudach", Tynar's Drudach was situated as the commercial trade center of the Eraré Sabban. It covered the western end of the sabban, abutting the Osiir Sabban. The streets leading through it allowed for goods to be conveyed from the docks, into the main trading areas of Tynar, and into the Grand Ward. And with wall-top byways, the druzirs and pashas could avoiding having to sully their feet upon its cobble. Besides official goods, bribery of the local amlakkhan allowed for contraband to travel through here and up to the Upper Muzad.

Tynar's Drudach was by far the busiest and most crowded of the three drudachs, not only because of its bazaars, but due its major temples and numerous private and public shrines.

In the 14 century DR, with the Sultan Tahyr as an absentee sabbalad the drudach was unofficially under the control of the Nine Pashas Trading Coster, who exerted their influence over many of the bazaar businesses surrounding their headquarters. At that time Tynar's Drudach had an ineffectual druzir, who was nothing more than a puppet of the Nine Pashas consortium, and the coster regularly bribed the sabban's vizar to look the other way.
Notable Locations
The Gauntlet Gardant A moderately fancy temple dedicated to Helm.
Ghasael Villa The three-story tall personal residence of Pasha Ghasael.
Lightning's Tower A moderately fancy black marble temple dedicated to Talos.
Modiminah's Villa Two luxury houses belonging to Pasha Modiminah, one standing five-stories tall and the other six-stories.
Nine Pashas Trading Coster Warehouses The Nine Pashas had five warehouses throughout Tynar's Drudach. The one closest to the Thaaleqab Khanduq was used to store armor, weapons, durable goods, and wagons.
Sabbaladah Dahaban The historic home and residence of the sabbalads of the Eraré Sabban. Following Sultan Tahyr's takeover of the position of sabbalad, the home was rented out to one of his favored fleet captains, Saibh el Milar.
House of Selim A moderately fancy house formerly belonging to a pasha, it was purchased in 1370 DR by Selim el Donar, captain of the Tynar's Drudach's amlakkhan, using the money from his promotion and the numerous bribes he took from both pashas and costers alike.
The Sorcerer's Hand An opulent temple dedicated to Azuth.
Thaaleqab Khanduq The headquarters of the Nine Pashas consortium.
Tehibi Villa The opulent two-story tall residence of the Pasha Tehibi.
Tynar's Square A open square near the center of Tynar's Drudach. It was flanked on three sides by The Gauntlet Gardant, Lightning's Tower, and The Sorcerer's Hand.
House of Wilam The two-story tall personal residence of Druzir Wilam el Loriln.

Osiir Sabban
Also regularly known as the "Harbor Sabban", for it was the sabban where all incoming captains had to register their ships and pay docking fees. It handled all management of the docks and harbor. And it was widely considered among sailors to be the entrance to Calimport, even when docking in one of the other Port Wards.

The sabban mark of Osiir was comprised of a silhouette of a single-masted ship with, full sails visible from the side. It was divided into three drudachs—Biguh Drudach, Piqaz Drudach, and Enqir Drudach.
Notable Locations
Kealza's Home The three-story guildhall of the Sail and Rope-Makers' League.Location: Biguh Drudach
House of Kemmel A fancy, four story tall building belonging to Kemmel, the druzir of the Biguh Drudach in the 14 century DR.Location: Biguh Drudach
Selamek's Warehouse A warehouse used by the Selamek's Scarlet Cross Trading Coster to store the various foods, silks, spices, and other fineries of Calimshan-make for later shipping up to Baldur's Gate. It also doubled as an official bazaar, with several tents and stalls pushed up against nearby buildings.Location: Enqir Drudach.
Shrine of St. Asref Situated in the small cellar apartment of a five-story tall row house, beneath the shop of a rope maker, this was a shrine begun by the Ilmatari priest Dolmas to honor the patron saint of the anti-slavery movement Nadhari.Location: Piqaz Drudach
Lighthouse of the Moon A temple of Selûne and literal lighthouse.Location: Piqaz Drudach
Temple of Old Night A nondescript shrine to the goddess Shar, it was one of five such buildings across Calimport that provided entrance to the Muzad and the true Temple of Old Night.Location: Enqir Drudach

History
Prior to Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal's establishment of wards as the city's largest sectors in the, Hook Ward was but part of what was known as the Dock Quarter.

Around the 12 century DR, during the Eighth Age of Calimshan, the fourth son of the last Pasha of the Eraré Dynasty was entombed alive within an unmarked tomb in the Muzad by an evil necromancer.

When a Rage of Dragons occurred in the, the continual bluish-white beacon of light emitted by the Lighthouse of the Moon by focusing the moon's rays attracted undue attention to Hook Ward one night, likely from the blue dragon Sapphiraktar.

When the Time of Troubles struck in, unleashing magical chaos across the Realms, the magic that had sealed the spirit of the Eraré prince failed and he escaped from his unmarked tomb as a wraith. Dubbed the "Eraré Wraith", this wrathful undead creature would prowl the shadowy streets of Calimport for years, until allegedly being destroyed by Javir yn Zamar el Hosaan in the, though some would continue to attribute the occasional mysterious death to the wraith.

## Calimport/Caravans Ward

The Caravans Ward was the ward of Calimport where the majority of caravan business and related enterprises were conducted. Due to its location in relation to other wards, it was considered to be technically both one of Calimport's four Port Wards and one of its eight Outer Wards.

Description
The Caravans Ward was situated on the eastern outskirts of Calimport, one of many areas that had once been enclosed by the Elder Wall in ancient times, abutting the shore east of Hook Ward. Those coming in from trade roads had to traverse  roundabout trails encircling the city until they could finally reach the staging grounds of the Caravans Ward.

It was a very grimy place, full of dust, dirt, and the constant foot traffic of beasts of burden. By the 14 century DR, the walls that partitioned the ward into sabbans were all in a state of dilapidation and lacked upper walkways, whilst the walls that partitioned its drudachs, much like those in many of the other Outer Wards, had long been trambled into mud. Because of this ill maintenance, the sabban walls were considered unfit byways by the upper classes. However, this was somewhat to the ward's advantage, as it made it one of the few areas in Calimport with large courtyards and wide avenues, perfect for assemblies of caravans.

In place of these walls, drudach boundaries were marked by small plinths, spaced apart by . Sabban markers were often placed at ground level, almost like stepping stones, spaced apart .

Government
In the 14th century DR, the Sultan of Caravans Ward was Kemar yn Kadadf el Dasanm. He was also the Pasha of the Guild of Excellent Drovers, Shepherds, and Animal Handlers and a senior member of the Mighty Guild of Bouncers, Laborers, and Sellswords. Working his way through the ranks of both guilds, as an oxen driver and caravan guard respectively, he managed to prove himself as a capable individual.

Recognizing himself as hardly amongst the smartest of sultans, Kemar entrusted most of his business affairs, as well as some negotiations, to the Syl-Vizar Conol yn Agar el Dasanm.

Defenses
Though the area was well guarded by the amlakkar, murders were not uncommon in the Caravans Ward. Particularly, murder of caravan drivers who failed to act according to the societal norms understood by the guilds and traders. The understood norms of the system were that one should not flaunt their wealth after a caravan shipment, nor should they refrain from promptly using those earnings to load up wagons with new goods for trade at the next city. These groups would seldom mourn those who died because of not knowing how to act in the system.

Furthermore, the amlakkar afforded to the Caravans Ward were not enough to ensure the safety of its cattle yards. Because of this, the Guild of Excellent Drovers frequently hired mercenaries to protect their penned cattle against wolves and other predators, especially those who were drawn towards the Pahlemm Sabban from the odors of its slaughterhouses.

Trade
Though the Caravans Ward wasn't conveniently situated near Calimport's main markets, as was the case for the staging grounds of so many other northern cities, trade good always managed to make their way to where they were needed through a system of intermediaries. Firstly, caravan drovers would sell to their guilds in the Thytos Sabban. These guilds would then sell it to an appropriate sales guild, such as the Grocers' and Farmers' Guild. Finally, these sales guilds would present the products within the markets of Calimport. And though this would result in markups, Calishites were accepting of the method, for it had long been the way in which business was conducted in Calimport.

Additionally, though the bulk of imports came in through the city's ports, a good deal of that shipped cargo was received by the Caravans Ward for shipment else. From the towns further inland to the north, to estates, and various other settlements, such as slave plantations and mining towns.

Sabbans
The Caravans Ward was divided into three sabbans and nine drudachs.
Drakhon Sabban
Also known as the "Stallions Sabban", was the definitive stables section of the ward. It was tucked against the walls of Hook Ward's shipyards, being adjacent to its Ajvent Sabban, as well as the Maker's Ward's Golnar Sabban. Its official name was derived from the Drakhon Dynasty of Calimshan.

Beyond stables, the Drakhon Sabban housed tanneries that crafted and sold tack, such as bridles and saddles, as well as many bazaars that sold and purchased horses and other exotic mounts, like displacer beasts and pegasi. The presence of these tanneries, coupled with the profusion of stables, made Drakhon a rather odorous sabban.

Among the more underprivileged caravan guards and attendants, the Drakhon Stable also served as an important rest stop. One where could rest at an inn, stock up on supplies, and find customers to buy the last of their caravan's goods. In some cases, they could even find themselves selling a full wagonload.

The sabban mark of Drakhon depicted a horse in silhouette. It was divided into three drudachs—Edaad Drudach, Hosaan Drudach, and the Meaza Drudach.
Notable Locations
Cattlemens' House The guildhall of the Guild of Excellent Drovers, Shepherds, and Animal Handlers.Location: Edaad Drudach
Nalihleb Villa Comprising two fancy buildings, one three-stories tall and the other stood four-stories, it was the private residence of Nalihleb, a pasha and the sabbalad of the Drakhon Sabban in the 14 century DR.Location: Hosaan Drudach
Silver Hoof Stables A lowclass business and stabling house.Location: Hosaan Drudach
The Veiled Lamia A combination festhall and inn that catered to caravan drovers and traders.Location: Meaza Drudach

Pahlemm Sabban
Also known as the "Oxen Sabban", was the section of Caravans Ward tied to the cattle industries of Calimshan's northern shanates. This included cattle yards towards its southern end, manure pits, some slaughter houses, and additional tanneries. The slaughter houses all sat on the outer reaches of the sabban, up against the walls of the Crypt Ward, so as to minimize disturbances to the public.

The sabban mark of Pahlemm depicted the head of a steer with large horns. It was divided into three drudachs—Gebna Drudach, Laban Drudach, and the Zebda Drudach.
Notable Locations
House of Dasanm An upscale, three-story tall house belonging to Pasha Dasanm.Location: Zebda Drudach
Kadar's Stables A lowclass stable.Location: Laban Drudach
Sayad Hill A prominent hill and plateau in the Pahlemm Sabban that was once the sight of a gate of the Elder Wall. Surrounding its base were a number of courtyards and staging areas, which drovers and trading caster organizers could look down upon from its top.
Temple of Old Night A nondescript shrine to the goddess Shar, it was one of five such buildings across Calimport that provided entrance to the Muzad and the true Temple of Old Night.
The Wagon House The guildhall of the Order of Skilled Wagonmakers and Coach Builders.Location: Gebna Drudach

Thytos Sabban
Nestled against the cliffs, the Thytos Sabban or "Court Sabban" as it was otherwise known, was the primary receiving area for caravans both entering and leaving Calimport. It was here where caravan drovers could sell their goods for resale by other parties.

The sabban mark of Thytos depicted a black wagon wheel. It was divided into three drudachs—Ba'ara Drudach, Krayim Drudach, and the Vifar Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Costerest The guildhall of the Carters, Coachmen, and Caravans Society.Location: Vifar Drudach
Izayad Villa Comprising two fancy buildings, one four-stories tall and the other stood five-stories, it was the private residence of Izayad, a pasha and the druzir of Ba'ara Drudach in the 14 century DR.Location: Ba'ara Drudach
The Nazullah The guildhall of the Trusted Order of Wheelwrights.Location: Krayim Drudach
Wind-Rider's Way A cloistered, long neglected bazaar and street, that was home to a shrine dedicated to Shaundakul.Location: Vifar Drudach

Inhabitants
A majority of Calimport's carters and drovers made their homes in the Caravans Ward, who exuded relatively relaxed moods and social attitudes, save for in times of unrest or when issues arose with the caravans. Aside from some pashas working in the ward as they had arisen from lowly ranks, few would ever dream of visiting this ward. Because of the aversion to this ward by the upper classes of Calimport, those on the run from the upper echelons of society often fled to and hid within the walls of the Caravans Ward.

It was not particularly safe to go wandering aimlessly through the ward, as it was said that those who got lost there could often end up finding themselves enslaved.

History
Prior to Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal's establishment of wards as the city's largest sectors in the, Caravans Ward was but part of what was known as the Craft Quarter.

## Calimport/Armada Ward

Armada Ward was the westernmost ward of the four Port Wards of the city of Calimport. Its enclosed docks comprised the naval portion of the wards, housing the armories, garrisons, and ships of el Nallojal, the navy of Calimshan.

Government
In the 14 century DR, the eldest son of Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal, Fahd yn Ralan el Pesarkhal, was the Sultan of the Armada Ward. In addition to other duties, he was also the Syl-Sultan of el Nallojal itself.

Sabbans
The Armada Ward was divided into two sabbans and six drudachs.
Djenispool Sabban
Though official documentation labeled it the Djenispool Sabban, most sailors and officers took care to refer to it only as the "Wharf Sabban" or more simply "The Wharf", due to the name being one of the few remnants of the prior ruling dynasty of Calimshan.

The sabban dominated 65% of the Armada Ward's total area, being composed of the docks proper and a few buildings, namely the ones that collected dock fees, the equipment warehouses of the League of Harbormasters, and a few minor businesses. Its docks could harbor two-thirds of the entire Nallojal fleet at any given time.

The sabban mark of Djenispool Sabban was a genie's lamp, prominently marked with a black six-pointed star, and pouring water out of its spout. It was divided into three drudachs—Fashol Drudach, Nahla Drudach, and the Nowm Drudach.

Notable Locations
The Harpoon Minaret A moderately fancy tower that functioned as the guildhall of the Guild of Fishermen, Whalers, and Undersea Hunters.Location: Nahla Drudach
Mohandis Villa Comprised of two fancy buildings, one three stories tall and the other four-stories, this villa was the private residence of Pasha Mohandis in the 14 century DR.Location: Fasol Drudach
Rabta Villa A sprawling mansion belonging to the Pasha Rabta. It was comprised three separate buildings, standing three, four, and six stories tall.Location: Nowm Drudach
The Wharf Amlakkhan The amlakkhan of the Armada Ward. It comprised two high-class buildings, one three stories tall and the other four stories.Location: Fasol Drudach

Tavihr Sabban
Also known as the "Hammock Sabban", this sabban comprised the armory and barracks of the naval armada. Its official name was derived from the Tavihr Dynasty, one of the more militaristic of the ancient bakkal dynasties of Calimshan. Its alternate title was derived from a unique facet of el Nallojal's garrisons—the bunks for seamen consisted of hammocks, two stories above the ground from ceiling beams and pillars. And in place of floors or stairs, the only way to get around were riggings and climbing ropes.The header text spells the name of the sabban as "Tavhir", yet says it is named for the bakkal dynasty, which is spelled "Tavihr". This spelling is also used under the names of notable locations, suggesting that the former was a misspelling.

Though it comprised only 35% of the ward's total area, it housed 90% of its buildings and businesses. Of these buildings, more than half were owned by the city and dedicated to the service of managing and coordinating el Nallojal. Many of the businesses in this sabban were operated by former Nallojal seamen. From them one could find almost any form of maritime service or support trade.

The sabban mark of Tavihr depicted a black anchor. It was divided into three drudachs—Hikal Drudach, Khadra Drudach, and the Seahrm Drudach.

Notable Locations
Bartoq Villa Composed of two fancy buildings, one two stories tall and the other three stories, this villa was the private residence of Bartoq, the sabbalad of the Tavihr Sabban in the 14 century DR.Location: Seahrm Drudach
House of Aban el Sirsi The three-story-tall private residence of Aban el Sirsi, a rysal and the druzir of the Khadra Drudach in the 14 century DR.Location: Khadra Drudach
The Nallojal Billets A garrison comprised of two buildings.Location: Hikal Drudach
Tomouh Villa Composed of two fancy buildings, one five stories tall and the other six stories, this villa was the private residence of Pasha Tomouh in the 14 century DR.Location: Khadra Drudach

Inhabitants
Whilst civilians were more than allowed to enter the Armada Ward, those looking to cause trouble were more than likely to get press-ganged into active service and shuffled off onto one of el Nallojal's ships for a tour of duty lasting three months. The only visitors that could avoid such a fate were those who had already voluntarily signed up for the navy and those that had connections to a pasha or someone of an even higher social ranking.

History
Around the year, the Drakhon Dynasty expanded and restructured the Armada Ward and other waterfront areas of Calimport that had been destroyed six years prior by the Villaflames conflagration. This would lead to the construction of the defenses and massive stone docks that would grace the ward for centuries to come. It was also around this period that Syl-Pasha Kamal el Drakhon commissioned the formation of El Qysanallojal.

Over the course of 1350 DR to 1370 DR, the Syl-Pashas of the El Djenispool and El Pesarkhal dynasties expanded upon the docks of Armada Ward, making it reach its two-thirds capacity. In particular, Syl-Pasha Rashid Djenispool commissioned much of the work done on the ward. He went on to become the namesake of the Djenispool Sabban and the only reason it would retain the Djenispool name in official documentation.

## Callie Brennan

Callie Brennan was a resident of Cormyr who lost their life in Lost Souls' Swamp.

Personality

Callie was sweet and kind, even though she was trapped as a cursed soul and had to talk to Evrim Whitehair.

History

While searching for her lost younger brother, Callie drowned while exploring an underground pool. The shadow of Lost Souls' Swamp trapped her soul there for its will-o'-wisps to feed on, along with Kyle Briarbuck and Evrim Whitehair. Though held by the efforts of the shadow's mudmen, vine horrors and wisps, their souls may have been freed by Harpers sent by Eradin Krall and Rina Belostos as they pursued Sshaastess and her Nether Scroll circa 1485 DR. Callie was able to explain that before she died, she had found a key to the ruins deeper in the cave, in which dwelled the predatory shadow. By finding her remains and the key, that would allow the Harpers to delve deeper and destroy the shadow once and for all.

## Calimport/Crypt Ward

Crypt Ward was the funeral district of Calimport and one of the city's eight Outer Wards. Popular colloquial names for the district among the locals included the "Dead Ward" or "Skulls Ward", as it had long been the site for tombs and mass burials, going as far back as the Sixth Age of Calimshan.

Description
Situated at the easternmost section of Calimport, this district was dominated by cemeteries, khamarkhas, markhouts, and temples. It had a great deal of shadowy alleyways and ordinarily empty avenues, perfect for the deplorable elements of Calimport to engage in illict activities and plot intrigues.

Government
In the 14th century DR, the eldest nephew of Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal through his brother Nasim, Muham yn Nasim el Pesarkhal, was the Sultan of the Crypt Ward. Considered a petty underachiever, the Syl-Pasha backhandedly bestowed this position upon Muham in order to keep him away from the affairs of court and its power players, referring to it as "a fitting reward for one of your ambitions".

Sabbans
Crypt Ward was divided into three sabbans and ten drudachs. Each of these sabbans were named for one of the noble houses of the pashas, whilst their colloquial names referred to the form of burial traditionally found in each sabban and its drudachs.
Adlel Sabban
Also known as the "Khamarkha Sabban" or the "Pasha's Rest Sabban", due to this northern sector of the Crypt Ward being dominated by the opulent mausoleums of the upper classes, along with towering monuments to their wealth and power. Numerous palm tree groves could be found among its walled courtyards, as well as many fountains that were magically maintained. For the upper class Calimpanni, the peaceful marble-paved avenues of the Adlel Sabban were considered as worthy of their presence as the byways atop sabban walls, the sabban as a whole being viewed as an elevated place in and of itself.

Its sabban mark was the sigil of House Adlel, a scimitar on the sinister (left-hand side) atop a cluster of three palm trees. It was divided into four drudachs—Nagaeh Drudach, Ovohl Drudach, Shamisad Drudach, and the Tunis Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Anhakhamarkha A massive marble khamarkha, topped with minarets, that was built in dedication to Syl-Pasha Abon III el Larau and his wife, Anha.Location: Shamisad Drudach
The Khamarnari A khamarka built for the Grand Vizar Samesaj. It was composed of solidified flames, which shifted in hue with the time of day.Location: Tunis Drudach
Nualorminoalh A temple dedicated to Oghma.Location: Ovohl Drudach
The Sahalarka The guildhall of the Fellowship Nykkar, Calimport's undertaker guild. This tower topped building also held a hidden shrine to whoever was the most prominent diety of death. By 1370 DR, the shrine was dedicated to Kelemvor.Location: Nagaeh Drudach

Irataq Sabban
Also known as the "Manycats Sabban" or the "Markhout Sabban", due to its abundance of individually, walled markhout tombs. This section of Crypt Ward was dedicated to the interment of merchants, pashas, and the middle class of Calimport society. Most of its markhouts were only a single story stall, the skies pierced by only few temple spires and some of the greater markhouts. Within these greater markhouts were kept the cremated remains of thousands, reposited within brass lamps packed in the floor and walls of the crypt.

Additionally, there were a number of markhouts in the sabban that were vacant. Said markhouts were clandestine connections between the surface and Calimport Muzad.

The sabban mark of Irataq depicted a cat's head. It was divided into three drudachs—Nasharot Drudach, Orbafura Drudach, and the Sabayn Drudach. The last of these three was almost commonly referred to colloquially as the "Drudach of the Seven Sons".
Notable Locations
Chathaodah The guildhall of the Skilled Circle of Butchers and Dressers.Location: Nasharot Drudach
The Dawn Belltowers An upscale temple dedicated to Lathander.Location: Orbafura Drudach
Osiirdah The guildhall of the Order of Hunters and Furriers.Location: Nasharot Drudach
Spectralhouse A tower and library full of on the undead. It belonged to one of the few Cloak Societies to persist following the fall of the Graycloak Society. This minaret was also the tallest buildings in Crypt Ward, looming above the the markhouts of the Irataq Sabban.Location: Sabayn Drudach

Kirruk Sabban
Also known as the "Mutar Sabban" or more disparagingly the "Forgotten Sabban", this section of the Crypt Ward was devoted to mass burials and the commoners of Calimport. Like the other sabbans, it too had a number of funerary monuments, though very few buildings, and fountains. Obelisks and small plinths marked its mass graves.

Where Kirruk Sabban stood out from the other two sabbans was in its lack of traditional drudach walls. In their place stood metal spear fences, which offered an unrestricted view into the sabban. Despite its "Forgotten" moniker and commoner ground, it was among the most popular public parks in Calimport around 1370 DR.

Unusually, the Kirruk Sabban lacked a sabban mark, for officials felt that its surroundings were so distinct from any other that there was no need for one. It was divided into three drudachs—Selamir Drudach, Tulamir Drudach, and the Zhakamir Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Darkness Passing A fancy temple dedicated to Kelemvor, though in centuries prior it had been a Myrkulyte temple.Location: Zhakamir Drudach
Stables of Tobeah A low-class stable and business.Location: Tulamir Drudach
Telamuzhidah A temple complex dedicated to Mask that had access to the Muzad. Around 1370 DR, it was notably being used as a secondary guildhall by the crime family El Kahmir.Location: Selamir Drudach
Temple of Old Night A nondescript shrine to the goddess Shar, it was one of five such buildings across Calimport that provided entrance to the Muzad and the true Temple of Old Night.

History
Prior to Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal's establishment of wards as the city's largest sectors in the, Crypt Ward was but part of what was known as the Craft Quarter.

Around the 11 century DR, an old Calimpanni practice of mass interring the middle class in brass lamps. By 1370 DR, five public markhouts had been filled with lamps of ashen remains.

In the late 14 century DR, Crypt Ward was growing a not too baseless reputation as a "Thieves' Quarter", a position that had been vacant in the city since thieves' guilds were run out of the Sholeh Sabban with the Darkstalker Wars. Not only did criminal factions and other rogues use the markhout facades in Irataq Sabban to travel between Calimport and Calimport Muzad, but Voraya of the Twisted Rune held a mesmeric influence over the young Sultan Muham, one which she used to her cabal's benefit.

In the month of Kythorn, in the, numerous crypts and khamarkhas were found either desecrated or destroyed over the course of a tenday. Coffins, along with the bodies that had been interred within them, were found missing. And in Kirruk Sabban, more than half of the mass graves showed signs of the ground being disturbed and sunken in, a potential sign that their corpses too had been stolen. One of the few pieces of evidence left behind by the culprits were mysterious claw marks in the drudach walls of Crypt Ward, as well as some parts of the walls being partially melted. The known necromancers in Calimport managed to produce alibis, proving they could not have been the ones responsible for the grave robbing. El Amlakkar, as well as bounty hunters hired by families of some of the affected deceased, would go on to scour the Port Wards for any signs of new arrivals with links to necromantic activities.
