## Calimport/Faiths Ward

The Faiths Ward was the foremost religious district of Calimport and one of the city's eight Outer Wards.

Description
One of the notable aspects of Faiths Ward was its buildings and architecture. More specifically, that most structures in the ward were still standing after more than a thousand years, despite living through the same sundry turmoil as the rest of the turbulent city—blazing fires, plagues, street battles between guilds, and street fights between criminals.

Many of the inns and taverns of the ward cater to the worshipers of specific faiths. This was often denoted by marking the requisite god's symbol upon the sign above a business's entrance.

Government
In the 14th century DR, the ruler of the Faiths Ward was Sultan Uarel yn Petal el Waukeen. As his name implied, the man was a member of the Church of Waukeen, as well as Pasha of the Guild of Money Lenders, Coinsmiths, and Pawn Brokers. His duties as Sultan rarely ever interfered with his ecclesiastical duties.

Sabbans
The Faiths Ward was divided into three sabbans and twelve drudachs.
Bakkal Sabban
Formerly known as "Joadhruz Sabban" and alternatively known by the moniker "High-Priests' Sabban", it was named for the bakkals, the ancient priest-rulers of Coramshan and later Calimshan during its First Age. Marked by a mixture of ancient and newer temples, it was most notable for the multitude of statues that dotted its streets and rooftops.

The sabban mark of Bakkal was that of a general face, topped with the sort of crown that the ancient bakkals wore, that of a coiled serpent. The sabban was divided into four drudachs—Ayal Drudach, Daid Drudach, Kariq Drudach, and the Masal Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Basilica of Night A magnificent temple dedicated to Shar. Once the seat of her power in Calimport, it was destroyed in -373 DR by the Sharrans themselves after it was taken over by Talontars.
The First Trader's Drink A small tavern that was a popular meeting place among the Waukeenar clergy.Location:  Kariq Drudach
The Fountain of the Qysars An open-air, octagonal palisade and fountain, covered by a glassteel dome. It was constructed in 194 DR, during the time of the Shoon Imperium. By 1370 DR, it was one of the few remaining intact structures from that regime. Fresh water could be drawn from the well, though attendant guards ensured that no one withdrew more than a cupful. A local tradition encouraged people to take vows and make alliances at the fountain, with both parties submerging their hands beneath its waters. According to legend, vows made in this fashion were bound by a curse created by the Shoon, one which would strike dead any who betrayed the vow made.Location: Kariq Drudach
The Imperious Flame A temple dedicated to Kossuth.Location: Ayal Drudach
The Measure House A luxurious temple dedicated to Anachtyr.Location: Masal Drudach
Minarets Guardant A temple dedicated to Helm.Location: Daid Drudach
Erehnir Sabban
Also known as "The Statue Sabban", due to the many carved or molded statues along its inner-facing brick walls. Most of these statues were of bakkals, posed in stoic positions, though a few were armed with weapons against opponents. By 1370 DR, much of the finer details on these statues had been worn away by the passage of time, though their rough outlines could all be made out.

Based on its name and wall of statuary, many assumed the Erehnir Sabban was constructed during the Erehnir Dynasty. In actuality, the wall was erected in honor of the Erehnirs following The Deepblaze of 911 DR, when it was the only sabban left untouched by the flames.

The Erehnir Sabban uniquely had no sabban mark, for it was felt by government officials that its inner-facing walls were so distinctive that it was impossible to confuse with any other. The sabban was divided into four drudachs—Ehlan Drudach, Enal Drudach, Farid Drudach, and Ghabbas Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Coinchapel One of two temples in Faiths Ward that were dedicated to the goddess Waukeen. Of the two it was the older structure and had a far more orthodox clergy, unwilling to accept Lliira's assumption of The Coinmaiden's divine duties.Location: Farid Drudach
The Counting House The guildhall of the Guild of Money-Lenders, Coinsmiths, and Pawn-Brokers.Location: Ehlan Drudach
Palace of the Murabirs A luxurious, walled estate of four domed buildings dating back to the Second Age of Calimshan. It was traditionally a ceremonial residence, provided to the three senior officers of the Qysaghanni and their families. The fourth of these houses merely served as an armory, housing some of the most powerful magical weapons the Qysaghanni had at their disposal to protect the Syl-Pasha with.Location: Ghabbas Drudach
The Shining Tankard A fairly new tavern in 1370 DR that catered to Lathanderites.Location: Ehlan Drudach
Evyrtaan Sabban
Otherwise known by the monikers "Dark Gods Sabban" and "Fallen Grace Sabban", for it had long been host to the greatest concentration of temples to evil deities in Calimport, the sabban's official name was likewise chosen for its negative connotations. That being the Evyrtaan Dynasty, whose ruler Syl-Pasha Orun yn Ymal acceded independence to the land of Tethyr.

Evyrtaan Sabban had a reputation as the most dangerous of the Faiths Ward's three sabbans and was considered by many to be unholy ground. However, despite this reputation, the sabban was host to a great number of businesses and drew in large swathes of coinage.

The sabban mark of Evyrtaan depicted the head of a hawk with a coin in its mouth. It was often abstracted in crude mosaics as something resembling concentric C's around a small gold dot. The sabban was divided into three drudachs—Ibran Drudach, Noal Drudach, and Samilar Drudach.
Notable Locations
Aurensahldah A luxurious two-building temple complex, dedicated to the goddesses Lliira and Waukeen. The larger and older of the two temples by more than 300 years was the one dedicated to Waukeen. The smaller temple was dedicated to Lliira, built sometime afterThe opening sentence for Aurensahldah declares it to be a temple dedicated to Waukeen and Chauntea, however, the rest of the text only discusses Waukeen and Lliira. For this reason, this article assumes that the mention of Chauntea was an error. the announcement of  by a Lliiran prophet that Waukeen was dead and Lliira was assuming her portfolio and duties.Location: Noal Drudach
The House Khateera Once a temple complex dedicated to Bane, following that god's destruction during the Time of Troubles it was bought out as a private residence by the merchant Maryn el Khateera. Unbenknownst to all, Maryn used his residence as a private shrine to Bane's son, Iyachtu Xvim.Location: Ibran Drudach
The Towers of Fury A large temple complex of four buildings, each dedicated to one of the Gods of Fury—Auril, Malar, Talos, and Umberlee. After centuries of temples to the Gods of Fury being destroyed by either divine or mortal acts, Syl-Pasha Saban el Djenispool had this complex constructed in 1356 DR.Location: Samilar Drudach

History
Prior to Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal's establishment of wards as the city's largest sectors in the, Faiths Ward was but part of what was known as the Temple and Learning Quarter.

In the summer of 320 DR, the Evyrtaan and Cajaan Sabbans become affected by the Infernal Death. The combusting bodies of the deceased cause a blaze that became known as the Plague Fires. Both sabbans ended up being temporarily gutted and abandoned.

In the, the Church of Lathander lead a zealous campaign against the churches of evil gods in the Bakkal Sabban. The arson they would commit would become known as the Zealot Fires. Over half of Bakkal Sabban would be engulfed in flames, with temples dedicated to Ibrandul, Shar, and Sharess being destroyed in the process.

Following the destruction of Bane in the, pandemonium swept amongst the orthodox Banites, the Cyricists, and the Maskarrans. The havoc in their wake would lead to the deaths of more than two hundred people and the destruction of several buildings in the Evyrtaan Sabban.

## Calimmon Garrisons

The Calimmon Garrisons were a series of major forts along the border of County Calimmon, the county of Tethyr's Duchy Ankaram that took up much of the border with Calimshan.

Description
The Garrisons were each an unimaginative but solidly built fortress situated atop a small hill and ringed with trenches ten to fifteen feet (three to five meters) deep. Their walls were between ten and fifteen feet thick and stood twenty feet (six meters) high. The garrisons themselves had between 10–15 officers and 200–300 soldiers under a fort commander, and each fort had different tactics and strategies according to its situation.

Geography
The forts were arrayed along the northern side of the River Agis between the Trackless Sea coast and the ruins of Shoonach. From west to east, the forts were Fort Agis near to Memnonnar and Daraqadim, Fort Tufenk in a southern bend of the river, Iltakar Garrison further up the river, and Fort Calim on the edge of County Monteshi, nearer to Shoonach and Fort Teqlar.

History
The Garrisons were over six centuries old by the time of the ascension of Zaranda Star following the Tethyrian Interregnum in the mid-14 century DR. Old Calishite claims on southwestern Tethyr—particularly Shoonach and Monrativi Teshy Mir in Duchy Ankaram—led to the ongoing threat of hostilities and land grabs, making the Calimmon Garrisons an important part of the border defenses managed by the Countess Kyrin Hawkwinter.

## Calimport/Hammer Ward

Hammer Ward was a ward of Calimport dedicated to all things metallurgy—armorsmiths, blacksmiths, and weaponsmiths—and was one of the city's eight Outer Wards. Whilst these three types of smiths could be found to varying degrees throughout the ward, each were typically sequestered to a dedicated sabban within its walls.

Location
This ward was located in the northeastern corner of Calimport. Hammer Ward was bordered to the west by Khanduq Ward's Kaval and Sholeh Sabbans. To the south it was bordered by the Adlel Sabban of Crypt Ward and the Nasim Sabban of Quill Ward.

Description
Throughout the ward one could hear the clammor of hammers striking anvils at all hours of the day, as well as often into the night. There was so much of this constant ringing that Quill Ward's abutting Nasim Sabban was referred to by some as an acoustic buffer between the two wards, ensuring that the smiths did not disrupt the tranquility of the latter's sages and scribes.

History
Prior to Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal's establishment of wards as the city's largest sectors in the, Hammer Ward was but part of what was known as the Craft Quarter.

In the, Syl-Pasha Pesarkhal broke ground on a long-term construction project, a defensive barrier he dubbed the Pesarkhal Wall, that would eventually encompass all of the Central Wards. In preparation for its eventual construction along Quill Ward, the Guild of Skilled Smiths and Metalworkers decided to demarcate its future placement by erecting a fence of tall, barbed metal spears along the sabban wall that separated Nasim Sabban and Hammer Ward's Tyrbos Sabban. These spears did nothing to obstruct passage along the sabban byways, but did make it very difficult to vault across into Nasim Sabban.

Government
In the 14th century DR, the ruler of Hammer Ward was Sultan Harel yn Rafam el Qardeen. Formerly a humble blacksmith, the man was bestowed this position by the Syl-Pasha after he inadvertently saved El Pesarkhal's life during the Darkstalker Wars.

Sabbans
The Hammer Ward was divided into three sabbans and twelve drudachs.
Amyran Sabban
Also known as the "Hammer Sabban", this sector of Hammer Ward was taken up by over fifty coarse smithies and workshops, producing common metalwork such as horseshoes and wheelrims. Here hardworking, commoner blacksmiths operated, who would say go went against the grain of the common Calishite work ethic.

Competition was fierce in this sabban, though there was always enough work to go around. There was also a strong sense of community amongst its inhabitants, working together to improve their community and sharing the goal of keeping their sabban free of the city's rampant corruption. This in turn made it a very safe place to live amongst Calimport's many sabbans.

The sabban mark of Amyran was a smith's claw hammer. It was divided into four drudachs—Atfa Drudach, Tefokh Drudach, Yistad Drudach, and Yistagga Drudach.
Notable Locations
The House of Five Rings The guildhall of the Guild of Skilled Smiths and Metalworkers.Location: Atfa Drudach
Sjûl Sabban
Also known as the "Anvil Sabban", for it was name was the Alzhedo word for anvil, this sector of Hammer Ward was dedicated to weaponsmiths. Under government ruling, weapon-makers needed to live closer to the heart of the city, so as to ensure that their wares could easily be put to use in defending the richer wards of Calimport.

Additionally, the True and Skilled Guild of Weapon-Makers ensured that all who operated here had to meet minimum standards of quality and were only permitted to sell two types of weapons in their shop, including such things as scimitars and spears. The latter restriction was put in place so as to ensure that no one weaponsmith could totally dominate Calimport's markets.

The sabban mark of Sjûl depicted an anvil in a circular field. It was divided into four drudachs—Nakhla Drudach, Roba Drudach, Sareef Drudach, and the Qima Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Dragon's Maw A popular festhall composed of two buildings, though uniquely joined by a tile facade to appear as one. It was renowned for its elaborate, ground level metal superstructure, a dragon's head and torso with wings that arced back to support its balconies.Location: Nakhla Drudach
Syrimatarah The guildhall of the True and Skilled Guild of Weapon-Makers.Location: Qima Drudach
Tyrbos Sabban
Also known as the "Ringing Step Sabban", was the primary home of skilled armorers and shield-makers, who much like the weapon-makers were required to live closer to the heart of the city. This sector of Hammer Ward was also home to blacksmiths of less larger metal wares. The bulk of their trade was in architectural pieces, such as the metal shingling that graced domes and minarets, door hinges, portcullises, and the grills and screens used in windows.

Due to the space needed for such smiths and the size of some of their products, Tyrbos Sabban boasted buildings that were larger than the norm, though it had fewer buildings overall. The majority of these structures were warehouses and three-story tall buildings. The latter of which were altered in their interior, making them merely two floor buildings, creating space on their ground floors for larger foundries and forges.

The name of the sabban was derived from the two tyrant Tyrbos pashas of the Second Age of Calimshan and its sabban mark was their sigil. This consisted of a chevron-shaped shield, placed off-center, and overlapping a dark circle. It was divided into four drudachs—Adifa Drudach, Harar Drudach, Maadan Drudach and the Zhakush Drudach.
Notable Locations
Hammersring Hall The guildhall of the Metalforgers Guild.Location: Maadan Drudach
Shield Hall The guildhall of the Rigid Order of Armorers and Shield-Makers.Location: Harar Drudach

## Calimport/Trades Ward

Trades Ward was the oldest mercantile sector of Calimport and was one of the city's eight Outer Wards. It was among the more profitable, if not prestigious, wards of the city.

Location
Located in the northwestern corner of Calimport, Trades Ward was sandwiched between Emerald Ward to the east and Faiths Ward to the west. To the south it was bordered by the Grand and Jewel Wards.

Description
The Trade Way directly entered Calimport through this ward, with its west side dominated by Bajhit Sabban.

Once guarded by the Elder Walls, Trades Ward's only remnant of this defensive barrier was the Malikhan Gates, whose entrances had long been blocked off and left to serve as a mere sightseeing piece for travelers. Trades Ward was also notable amongst the wards for having the highest concentration of taverns outside of the Port Wards.

Government
In the 14th century DR, the twelfth son of Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal, Faruk yn Ralan el Pesarkhal, was the Sultan of Trades Ward, astonishingly rising to the position at the mere age of eighteen.

Trade
By the, Trades Ward continued to thrive as the main area of mercantile business with the northern shanates (outlying estate farms).

Sabbans
Trades Ward was divided into three sabbans and eleven drudachs.
Bajhit Sabban
Also known as "The Tent Sabban", this outskirts sector of Trades Ward was made up of a disorganized bazaar and tents, centered around the ancient Malikhan Gates, which far outnumbered the few brick buildings in the sabban. Home to a sizable impoverished section of the Calimpanni populace, those traveling by Bajhit Sabban were given the impression that Calimport was a chaotic city. And any who traveled at ground level, more  away from the Grand Gate, were oft swarmed by pickpockets. Yet a semblance of peace was managed in the sabban, thanks to a combination of its walls and amlakkhans.

Its sabbalad in the 14 century DR was Pasha Amahd el Sufontis.

The sabban mark of Bajhit consisted of four slashes, making a sort of crude tent shape. It was divided into four drudachs—Barra Drudach, Khayef Drudach, Sukan Drudach, and the Tlaen Drudach.
Notable Locations
The lumaldah A combined guildhall and warehouse belonging to the Order of Offal-Movers and Dungsweepers.Location: Barra Drudach
Sadufah's Tannery The guildhall of the Guild of Skinners, Tanners, and Leather-Workers.Location: Khayef Drudach
Sufontis Market A khanduq with an indoor bazaar. Owned by House Sufontis, it was surprisingly well-kept for the area and provided a variety of services.Location: Tlaen Drudach
The Twelve Ovens The guildhall of the Bakers' Guild.Location: Sukan Drudach
Ylar's House The guildhall of the Order of Bricklayers and Brickmakers.Location: Tlaen Drudach
Larau Sabban
Also known as the "Arena Sabban" or "Games Sabban", for nearly all aspects of business and life in this northeastern sabban were tied in one way or another to the Djen Arenas, the two foremost arenas of Calimport. These structures were so imposing, they could be seen from sabban walkways up to three sabbans away. Larau Sabban was named for the Larau, a family of qysars during the reign of the Shoon Imperium who were big proponents of the Djen Arenas.

It was one of the two sabbans that primarily attracted visitors to Trades Ward. No matter the time of day, it was by far the busiest of the three. And the cacophony of cheering crowds was audible all across its expanse.

Fitting its central focus, the sabban mark of Larau was an elongated oval, reminiscent of the shape of the arenas. At the center of this oval was set a trident. It was divided into four drudachs—Khamar Drudach, Mirab Drudach, Niqal Drudach, and the Shomuz Drudach.

Notable Locations
The Arena Efreetum One of the two Djen Arenas. It was the easternmost arena and didn't charge for entry regardless of one's station in society, due to a tradition in which visitors would "vote" on a winner by flinging coins at the combatant they wished to see lose.Location: Shomuz Drudach
The Arena Sabam One of the two Djen Arenas. It was the westernmost arena, the larger of the two, and charged visitors for entry.Location: Mirab Drudach
The Arms House A temple dedicated to Tempus. Situated close to the Djen Arenas, it acted a sort of secondary barracks for the gladiators.Location: Shomuz Drudach
The Golden Goblet A tavern that was notable for being the progenitor of the renowned Golden Sands Brewery, the first of over three hundred franchises that they would come to establish all across Calimport and wider Calimshan.Location: Niqal Drudach
Trident's Rest A tavern not affiliated with the Golden Sands that was noted for its wide range of beverages from across the Realms. It managed to eschew pressure from them due to its magical protections and the owner's close connections to members of the ruling class.Location: Khamar Drudach

Sahar Sabban
This sector of Trades Ward was centered on the brewing, distilling, and vinting of beverages. Most services in the sabban were under the control of the Vintners', Distillers', and Brewers' Guild. And it was one of two sabbans that primarily attracted visitors to Trades Ward.

Sahar Sabban was colloquially referred to as the "Golden Sands Sabban", for two out of its three drudachs were dominated by the Golden Sands, which expanded here after it outgrew The Golden Goblet. Golden Sands had close ties to both El Vyndahla and the Brewers' Guild, whose guildmaster Tasyn el Effyd was also the the ruling sabbalad in the 14 century DR. He maintained the inequity of this situation, being more than happy to improve his profits by forcing people out of Sahar Sabban, or into an overcrowded drudach.The text refers to an overcrowded "Qinae Drudach", however, no such area by this name appears throughout either the text or maps of the sourcebook Calimport.

In opposition to the Golden Sands' near monopoly on alcoholic beverages, black marketeers were turned to by the public to meet an ever growing demand for other ales and wines.

The name of the sabban was derived from House Sahar and its sabban mark was once their sigil. This was later replaced with a depiction of a goblet, with three red drops spilling over its rim. It was seperated into three drudachs. The Coniq Drudach and Jhafer Drudachs, which colloquially had collective name of "Golden Sands Drudachs", and the Zeqra Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Chawal's Bridle A stables business.Location: Jhafer Drudach
The Golden Sands Brewery A complex of buildings stretched across the Coniq and Jhafer Drudachs. Altogether these brewing, preparatory, and distilling buildings produced more ale, beer, and wine than any other single producer in Faerûn.
The Shanates' Bounty The guildhall of the Grocers' and Farmers' Guild.Location: Zeqra Drudach
Sunned Barley Villa The guildhall of the Vintners', Distillers', and Brewers' Guild. Its main building fronted the wall of Sahar Sabban.Location: Coniq Drudach

History
Prior to Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal's establishment of wards as the city's largest sectors in the, Trades Ward was but part of what were known as the Market Quarter and Temple and Learning Quarter.

Sometime after 100 DR, during the reign of the Shoon Imperium, the Trade Way from Athkatla to Calimport was constructed, cementing Trades Ward's future importance to the city.

In the summer of, much of Larau Sabban is set ablaze during the Caravan Fires incident, as fighting breaks out amongst trade factions in eastern Calimport amidst droughts.

Early in the month of Tarsakh, in the  Sabbalad Amahd el Sufontis passes away. Various family members and heirs begin fighting over his estate, including his real estate and trade holdings. People fear that street warfare may be soon to follow in Sahar Sabban.

## Calimport/Emerald Ward

Emerald Ward was one of the Outer Wards of the city of Calimport, the capital of Calimshan. A newer, tidier, and grander ward compared to others, following devastating fires, it became the abode of rising merchants.

Location
Lying on the northern side of the city, Emerald Ward was sandwiched between the Trades Ward on the west and the Khanduq Ward on the east, with the Grand Ward to the south.

Description
As its name implied, Emerald Ward was one of the first sights travelers had of the riches and luxuriousness of Calimport as they journeyed down the Trade Way from the north. Standing in stark contrast to the dirt and desperation of parts of the neighboring Trade Ward and other areas of Calimport, Emerald Ward of around 1370 DR was cleaner, more recently built, and more ostentatious, thanks to the rebuilding effort after the fires devastated this area of the city only a few years before. The grand buildings here sported a dazzling profusion of bright-hued paints and tiles. The old bazaars also expanded into the cleared areas, becoming more spacious marketplaces like those seen in northern cities.

As such, it was the residence of many of the up-and-coming merchants of Calimport's Outer Wards and an Emerald Ward address marked this to the rest of the city. Such folk were 'new money' and the uppermost of the lesser classes—if not the peak, then near to it. They competed in social matters and in building taller villas and businesses.

History
The area was formerly a part of Calimport's Market Quarter, before Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal established the system of wards in the .

However, in the, the Trades Conflagration blazed across northern and central Calimport. The cause was unknown but rumored about: some attributed the fires to smokepowder shipments being transported through the overcrowded bazaars of Marekh Sabban, and others blamed Mystrans and Cyricists for fighting in the streets. In any case, it was concentrated in that sabban and it wiped out the old bazaars, row houses, and khanduqs. By the time the fires were out, it had burned 60% of the Emerald Ward and razed the entire Marekh Sabban, as well as countless areas of the Muzad undercity. The temples of Cyric, Mystra, and Sune in Marekh were destroyed and many who lived there had perished.

Nevertheless, work was underway on rebuilding much of Marekh Sabban by early 1370 DR. Taking advantage, landowners bought up large stretches of land in Marekh and neighboring parts once belonging to deceased residents. Many businesses and homeowners in neighboring Khanduq Ward, which was also affected by the fires, even moved into Emerald Ward or near its boundary as they could.

Government
Circa 1370 DR, Emerald Ward was controlled by Sultan Nasim the Younger, the favorite nephew of Ralan el Pesarkhal, the ruler of Calimshan. He was loyal and considered equal in talent to the sultan of the neighboring Trades Ward, his cousin Faruk, but to prefer business to crime, though he did have a gambling habit. He did not exert much control on use of the land.

A rival to Nasim was Husuf el Halid, the spendthrift son of a wealthy moneylender and the local nirdey, or chief collector, of the Rundeen that dominated local merchants.

Sabbans
Emerald Ward was divided into three sabbans and ten drudachs.

Axash Sabban
An ever-bustling space, Axash Sabban had the largest marketplace for clothing, from the most mundane to the most extravagant, so it was often called the Cloth Sabban or Sash Sabban. However, because of such competition, the tailors and sellers often take their business and best items into the Grand Ward or Palace Ward, the better to sell straight to the wealthy pashas and sultans.

The sabban mark for this sabban was three sashes, represented by three wavy parallel lines. It contained three drudachs: Eyer, Gagi, and Wahir.In Calimport, p. 40, Eyer Drudach is listed in both Axash and Otahl Sabbans. The latter is presumed to be in error, based on the city-wide map of Calimport and its sabbans on p. 29.

Notable Locations
 The Tower Sufontis  A five-story minaret tower and the home of House Sufontis.Location: Eyer Drudach; #7
 Samarkhan's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Samarkhan with two- and four-story buildings.Location: Eyer Drudach; #8
 Capridah  The three-story home of Khiber el Wisynn, the night-watch commander of the Great Bazaar's minaret guards. It had a crypt in the cellar.Location: Gagi Drudach; #11
 The Dao's Step  Guildhall of the Cobblers' Society.Location: Wahir Drudach; #12
 Rasûla's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Rasûla with two- and four-story buildings.Location: Wahir Drudach; #15
 The Sultry Siren  A lavish four-story festhall controlled by the Jhasinnar Sodality.Location: Gagi Drudach; #18

Marekh Sabban
Also called the Black Sabban and later the Great Bazaar Sabban, Marekh Sabban was largely destroyed in the Trades Conflagration. Once it held countless bazaars, khanduqs, and hundreds of row houses, as well as temples to Mystra, Sune, and Cyric—all were destroyed. Instead, it was actively being rebuilt as of 1370 DR. The six minarets surrounding the Great Bazaar were among the first to be erected, though it was yet to gain any new temples.

The sabban's whole western half came to be covered by open market, called the Great Bazaar. It permitted temporary stalls for periods of 12 hours in either day or night, enabling 24-hour business. The majority of goods traded here were daily foods, common spices, and other essentials. The market was controlled by Pasha Sufontis. The rest of the sabban was owned by a dozen major families and more than a hundred individual merchants and business owners.

The sabban mark for this sabban was a seven-pointed star within a circle of seven coins, with a coin at each point. It contained four drudachs: Azhaya, Maz'ahl, Yeaz, and Yeroh.

Notable Locations
 Best Harps Hall  Guildhall of the Innkeepers Society, boasting five stories.Location: Maz'ahl Drudach; #1
 Yzhan's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Yzhan with two-story buildings.Location: Maz'ahl Drudach; #2
 The Pearls  The home of Vanda Volahrn, a mage and one of the few female pashas in Calimport. Her house reached three stories and had an outer walled yard.Location: Azhaya Drudach; #3
 Bhinasal's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Bhinasal, it had three- and four-story buildings.Location: Yeroh Drudach; #4
 Akhadar's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Akhadar, it had three- and four-story buildings.Location: Yeaz Drudach; #5
 Yekhol's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Yekhol with two-story buildings.Location: Yeroh Drudach; #6

Otahl Sabban
Also known as Tumahl's Sabban, this sabban was most famous as the birthplace and residence of the pirate Tumahl el Otahl, the Rogue Son of El Otahl, a legendary adventurer of the Eighth Age of Calimshan. A large white marble statue of him stood in the center of the biggest bazaar in the sabban, pointing a scimitar to the southwest, either toward the Pasha's Sabban or the Armada Ward docks as a challenge to the two figures with which Tumahl had most contended.

The sabban mark for this sabban was a slender dagger with no guard and a hole in the base—this, too, was the signature of Tumahl el Otahl. It contained four drudachs: Farix, Khumil, and Mabul.

Notable Locations
 Seven Chalices Trading House  Guildhall of the Kindly Order of Silversmiths.Location: Farix Drudach; #9
 Schamazharkh's house  The home of Tulan el Galin, the druzir of Khumil Drudach and an important member of the Circle of Architects, Engineers, and Builders. Naturally, his house had three stories with an adjoining four-story minaret.Location: Khumil Drudach; #10
 The Halls of Fortune  A temple to Tymora.Location: Farix Drudach; #13
 Baalaed's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Baalaed with two- and four-story buildings.Location: Khumil Drudach; #14
 Sha'al's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Sha'al with two-story buildings.Location: Mabul Drudach; #16
 Awadabh's villa  The high-class villa of Pasha Awadabh with three- and four story buildings.Location: Mabul Drudach; #17

## Calimport/Khanduq Ward

Khanduq Ward was a mixed-focused sector of Calimport and one of the city's eight Outer Wards.

Description
Khanduq Ward got its name from the abundance of khanduqs and marketplaces scattered throughout it.

It once had a connection to Quill Ward through the Hapij Sabban, however, at somepoint it was sealed shut.

Government
In the 14th century DR, the Sultan of Khanduq Ward was Daud yn Daud el Vehmet. He was a rather young ruler, barely past 20 years of age in 1370 DR, and was also the pasha of the Spicemonger Fellowship.

Trade
By the 14th century DR, much of the business and trade that Khanduq Ward had once been privy to had shifted westward into the adjacent Emerald Ward.

Sabbans
Khanduq Ward was divided into three sabbans and ten drudachs. These sabbans were unofficially "segregated" into sectors that focused on business, entertainment, and residence respectively.
Kaval Sabban
Also known as "Tuamir's Sabban" or "the Sabbazaar", was the trade focused sector of Khanduq Ward. Residential buildings were absent in this sabban, for khanduqs occupied more than half of the available land, with the rest taken up by the khanduqs' street bazaars. At sunset all within Kaval Sabban would be cleared out and its gates would be locked shut. During the night a contingent of twelve amlakkars were stationed along its walls at night, whilst another contingent of twelve would patrol the interior for rogues, eventually swapping posts with the wall-guards.

Its colloquial nickname was in reference to Tuamir, an infamous rogue back in the 11 century DR who ran a far reaching thieves' guild from down in Calimport Muzad.

The sabban mark of Kaval was the old symbol of Tuamir, an eye an bisected by a vertical, downward facing arrow. It was divided into four drudachs—Aruv Drudach, Rhamal Drudach, Qelt Drudach, and Syral Drudach.
Notable Locations
Khanduq of the Coinmother A marketplace and the city's foremost temple of Waukeen, rivaling other Waukeenar temples in Faiths Ward. Its high priest in the 14 century DR was Pecal el Saiduwm, the Druzir of Syral Drudach.Location: Syral Drudach
Taanith's Khanduq A khanduq and guildhall that was shared by the Esteemed Guild of Builders and the Circle of Architects, Engineers, and Planners.Location: Rhamal Drudach
The Treant's Khanduq The guildhall of the Fine Wood Carvers Order. It stood out from many other buildings in the sector due to being made entirely out of wood.Location: Aruv Drudach

Naiid Sabban
Also known as "Pomartal's Sabban", was the entertainment focused sector of Khanduq Ward. It was replete with clusters of festhalls, inns, taverns, and gambling establishments.

Its colloquial nickname was in reference to Pomartal, a balak who was sworn enemies with Tuamir back when it was a more lawful sabban. Ever since his death to assassins one night in the, Pomartal's ghost walked the byways of Naiid Sabban's walls, punishing any criminals he caught in the act.

The mark of this sabban was the ancient signet of Pomartal, scales of justice balanced upon the upper tip of a lightning bolt. In mockery of the lawfulness that the ward once stood for, members of the entertainment industries and their clients marred and graffiti this mark in many places. The one exception to this was an area known as Pomartal's Walk.

Naaid Sabban was divided into three drudachs—Balamhir Drudach, Tanradh Drudach, and Yuam Drudach.
Notable Locations
Miatarra The guildhall of the Spicemonger Fellowship.Location: Tanradh Drudach
The Minarets Muzhadahr A luxurious temple that was once dedicated to Bane. Following the Time of Troubles, it became a house of Cyric worship.Location: Yuam Drudach

Sholeh Sabban
Also known as "Felin's Sabban", was the residential sector of Khanduq Ward. It was a horribly overcrowded place, with row houses crammed full of three times their expected capacity. And many of its ancient khanduqs and villas were occupied by destitute squatters. Its name was likely derived from the Sholeh Dynasty.

What would become known as Sholeh Sabban was originally built in the Forth Age of Calimshan, early into the Vihad Dynasty. During that time, spanning the course of five Vihad pashas, the area was protected by a powerful mage known as Felin. Under his vigilant watch, harm never befell the area's structures nor its people. After his death and covert burial in Calimport Muzad in -496 DR, people would continue to say they felt his protective, ghostly presence. And indeed, ever since that time, Sholeh Sabban was never once devastated by fires.

The area would later gain a reputation as the "Thieves' Quarter" of Calimport, beginning around the 9 century DR, and this would be the state of things for over five centuries. The underworld presence in Sholeh disintegrated in 1359 DR, as the Djenispool Dynasty fell and the underworld was fractured by the chaos of the Darkstalker Wars. Ever since that conflict, the ward had been free of thieves' guilds.

The sabban mark of Sholeh was modeled after the mage sigil of the ancient wizard Felin, being composed of an hourglass that was centered over a quintet of five-pointed stars. The sabban was divided into three drudachs—Denos Drudach, Eachid Drudach, and Sarkh Drudach. This last one in particular was known by some collquially as the "Rogues Drudach".
Notable Locations
Pook's Palace The home of the infamous Pasha Pook, a crimelord who used to have wide-reaching influence over the assassins' and thieves' guilds of Calimport, as well as the guildhall of the Pook guild. Whilst described by some having once been an opulent villa, this opulence was relegated to its interior, as the exterior looked to be little more than a wooden warehouse without any balconies or terraces. After Pook's criminal enterprise fell apart in 1357 DR, Sabbalad Nur yn Aban el Esarn took up residence in the structure and allowed it to fall into a state of partial disrepair.Location: Sarkh Drudach
The Protector's Tower An ancient wizard tower that had once belonged to the renowned Felin. It was magically protected structure that managed to keep out all trespassers over the centuries, leaving it a mystery as to what treasures it held inside.Location: Denos Drudach
Rogues Circle An open cul-de-sac, at the end of which lied Pook's Palace.
The Spitting Camel A low-class tavern and inn along Rogues Circle.Location: Eachid Drudach
Temple of Old Night A nondescript shrine to the goddess Shar. It was one of five such buildings across Calimport that provided entrance to the Muzad and the true Temple of Old Night.

History
The area was formerly part of what was known as the Market Quarter, before Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal established the system of wards in the,

Sometime after the Djenispool regime of Calimshan was established in 1187 DR, the pashas eradicated the subterranean power base of Tuamir's guild by collapsing parts of Kaval Sabban atop it. They would go on to rebuild that portion of the sabban atop those ruins.

In 1357 DR, the Companions of the Hall traveled all the way from the Sword Coast to Calimport in effort to rescue their friend Regis from Pasha Pook and his guild of thieves. In the month of Eleasias they would reach the city and travel into the sector of Market Quarter that would later become Khanduq Ward. There they rested until night at the Spitting Camel Inn, making note of how the cul-de-sac it was on, Rogues Circle, became even more packed with activity. At night they went out and the barbarian Wulfgar pried open one of the many iron grates that lined the street, making their way down into the sewers of Calimport, in hopes of sneaking into Pook's Palace. However, in those depths they found themselves face to face with Calimport Muzad's wererat denizens. Later on, after they had brought an end to Pasha Pook, Drizzt Do'Urden would look out upon the nightly streets of the area and remark to himself how things seemed suspiciously quiter, a sense of growing anticipation at the conflict to come over the power vacuum he left.

During the Darkstalker Wars of 1359 DR, due in part to arcane forces unleashed by the infamous Jarlaxle and his allies, as well as his opponents, like the Dark Daggers, the streets of Sholeh Sabban were faced with the destruction of a few buildings and over 2,000 deaths.

In the, Calimport was wracked by the Trades Conflagration. Whilst an outstanding portion of damages would be suffered by Emerald Ward, much of the western quarter of Naiid Sabban would also be hit by the blaze. However, unlike Emerald Ward, the shells of much of Naaid's buildings and older khanduqs would be left intact. Over the next year, the sabban would be met with a flurry of bidding wars over real estate, as many flocked to gain ownership of one of the partially built homes and businesses that abutted Emerald Ward.

## Calmishandra

Calmishandra was a wizard residing in Stag Falls during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Abilities
Between her and the cleric of Torm Gunther, they'd cast continual light, magic mouth, and alarm spells to guard the Stag Falls castle.

History
Calmishandra lived in the castle at Stag Falls until the vampire Romanisk Vlaensk took over the town. She had helped bolster castle defenses.

## Cassandra (Stag Falls)

Cassandra was a serving wench in Stag Falls in the Vast during the mid-to-late 14 century DR.

Activities
She worked for Baron Vilhelm von Stag Falls, against whom she organized an underground resistance within his castle, meager though it was, once he became an undead.

History
After Baron Vilhelm von Stag Falls was turned into an undead creature by the vampire wizard Romanisk Vlaensk, he set about the task of mind-controlling his castle staff. But when he tried this on Cassandra, it failed, though he failed to notice it. Since then, she, and the few guards that managed to endure the effect, secretly worked to undermine him.

When adventurers came to Stag Falls and tried to investigate the castle, Cassandra likely assisted them if they went to the kitchen. She would also likely have aided them if they were imprisoned in the castle, by sneaking them a key and a note, or knocking out the jailer with the help of a few free-willed guards.

A minority of people from Stag Falls thought she should become the new baroness after the destruction of Vilhelm von Stag Falls' undying form, as she'd organized what resistance had been held. Though they were vocal, others thought her not being charmed was merely an accident.

## Calimport/Grand Ward

Grand Ward was an upper-class district of Calimport, considered the second richest of all the wards, and was one of the city's seven Central Wards.

Location
As its classification implied, Grand Ward was a centralized part of Calimport. To the north it was bordered by the Axash Sabban of Emerald Ward, the Naid and Sholeh Sabbans of Khanduq Ward, and the Sahar Sabban of Trades Wards. It was sandwiched between Quill Ward to the east and Jewel Ward to the west. And to the south it bordered the Ylar Sabban of Dock Ward.

History
The area was formerly part of what was known as the Market Quarter, before Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal established the system of wards in the . superseding the long-standing system of sabbans and drudachs. Leading up to this point, over the course of a few centuries, the areas that would be delineated as the Grand, Jewel, and Palace wards underwent vertical construction by the Circle of Architects, Engineers, and Builders. This was done with the intention of providing both the upper classes and their servants greater areas of mobility, as well as to keep the latter out of sight.

In the, the Trades Conflagration blazed across northern and central Calimport. The cause was unknown but rumored about: some attributed the fires to smokepowder shipments being transported through the overcrowded bazaars of Jewel Ward's Marekh Sabban, and others blamed Mystrans and Cyricists for fighting in the streets. In any case, though the fires were largely concentrated in that sabban, they would spread over to Grand Ward. By the time the fires were out, the conflagration had engulfed 50% of Grand Ward, having affected Cajaan Sabban and Casajr Sabban.

Much of the real estate in the ward was cleared and would only be rebuilt by 1370 DR. In the wake of this rebuilding, Grand Ward's Cajaan Sabban had become the largest market area in Calimport.

Government
In the late 14th century DR, the Sultan of Grand Ward was Perat el Zasta. He was among the many "new money" Calimpanni at that time, having moved over from the Wizard Ward.

The Sabbalad of Makista Sabban, Fahd yn Ralan el Pesarkhal, was notably the holder of the office of Sultan of Armada Ward.

Inhabitants
The residents of Grand Ward were affluent individuals, possessing such wealth that they could live idle lives. An address in the ward was considered a sure sign that one had reached the upper class in Calimport. However, they were looked upon with disdain by the residents of Palace Ward as being "new money" upstarts.

The lower level of the ward, out of sight of the upper classes, was reserved for their servants and slaves. Life here largely operated as any other part of Calimport, but due to its obscured nature many sultans, pashas, and the like conducted clandestine activities there with the city's criminal powers.

Sabbans
Grand Ward was divided into four sabbans and thirteen drudachs. However, much like its neighbors, the distinctions between these sabbans and drudachs was blurred due to its layered infrastructure.

The slightly vaulted, stonework secondary layer of Grand Ward was the "ground level" to its rich denizens. Braced by both stone and timber supports, it was comprised of solid street avenues and courts, granting the upper classes more uninterrupted movement than the sabban-wall byways afforded. The engineers responsible constructed it in such a manner as to ensure that it would stay elevated even if half of these timber supports were broken. One could access the city's true ground level and vice-versa by traversing sets of stairs.

The edges of the ward's byways, the primary "roads" upon which moneyed folk traveled across the lengths of Calimport, served as the "curbs" of this layer. As the boundary defining sabban marks were not present on the second layer, those that walked its elevated streets used the glazed coloration of these curbs to determine which sabban and drudach they were standing in. Each were assigned a distinct coloration, with the latter being denoted as a stripe at the base of the sabban color.

The lower level of Grand Ward was often lumped together with those of the Jewel and Palace wards as the "Upper Muzad", being considered the uppermost layer of the Muzhahajaarnadah. In some areas there were even said to be hidden entrances to the Muzad. With the sky blocked out by the elevated streets, save for stairwells and the gates to the open-air Outer or Port Wards, torches had to be relied upon for illumination.

Cajaan Sabban
Also known as the "Market Sabban", was the central mercantile sector of the ward. Its most defining feature was the Cajaan Market, which had significantly expanded in scope following the Trades Conflagration.

The sabban mark of Cajaan was composed of a fiery sun, pierced from behind by three arrows that were all pointed southwest. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was green, whilst the colors of its drudachs were crimson red, midnight blue, and wheat yellow.It is not specified anywhere within the text which color each drudach is associated with. The three drudachs that made up the sabban were Dabun Drudach, Mit'adh Drudach, and Semalej Drudach.
Notable Locations
The four marble khanduqs A group of khanduqs composed of marble that were destroyed in the Trades Conflagration. They had stored vast sums of gold, which were melted by the heat of the conflagration, pouring down into the Muzad to be collected by the undercity's denizens of dubious repute. This gold amounted to 10,000 gp and 2,500 trade bars.
House of Warig A luxurious four-story tall house belonging to Pasha Wariq, the Sabbalad of Casajr and the Druzir of Semalej Drudach.Location: Semalej Drudach
The Violivery The guildhall of the Quiet Order of Stablemasters, Farriers, and Grooms.Location: Dabun Drudach
Villa Ozar A luxury residence belonging to Pasha Ozar.Location: Mit'adh Drudach
Casajr Sabban
Also known as the "Stars Sabban", was largely dominated by the entertainment business, as well as some more scholarly trades.

Nearly a third of the sabban was set aflame during the Trades Conflagration due to its warehouses, which held large stocks of ink, parchment, and vellum used by the Dutiful Circle of Binders and Printers and the Masterful Order of Clerks, Scribes, and Scriveners. The libraries of the sabban were luckily spared any damage.

The sabban mark of Casajr depicted a book, with a five-pointed star on its outer cover. The prominent point of this star was always facing up. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was slate gray, whilst the colors of its drudachs were ivory, sky blue, and tan. The four drudachs that made up the sabban were Baela Drudach, Farag Drudach, Vihat Drudach, and Zhamur Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Bakkals' Dial A massive brass sundial that rested within the pavement of a street square. Dating back to circa -1130 DR, its location was moved several times over the centuries as Calimport faced all manner of catastrophies. By the late 14 century DR, the only noticeable damage The only damage to the landmark was a large crack through the southern third of the dial, though this had no adverse affect on its ability to measure the time of day.Location: Zhamur Drudach
The Bindery The guildhall of the Dutiful Circle of Binders and Printers.Location: Vihat Drudach
House of Saralon A moderate three-story house belonging to Pasha Saralon.Location: Farag Drudach
Minaret of the Sage Khumal A wizard-tower belonging to the mage Khumal.Location: Baela Drudach

Makista Sabban
Also known as the "Golden Maidens Sabban", was a relatively ordinary sabban. It had the jumble of row houses and shops that one would expect of any Faerûnian city, constructed of either glazed mud-brick or carved stone, though they dealt only in expensive luxury wares. It was a particularly ancient part of Grand Ward, with some saying that its winding streets had been put in place farther back than the measurable lifetime of a dragon.

The carts and tents that made up the sector's bazaars, whilst impermanent in most other parts of Calimport, were permanent fixtures of Makista. And the sub-streets of the sabban winded precariously around khanduqs and other buildings. Due to the layout of these streets making it difficult to engage in a pursuit, both layers of Makista Sabban were prized by thieves and pickpockets alike.

The nickname and mark of the sabban were both derived from a particularly renowned festhall that had been around since the 9 century DR. It was composed of four outlines of female figures, arranged in a cross-pattern, with their feet pointing together and merging. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was yellow, whilst the colors of its drudachs were ash gray, black, and sea green. The three drudachs that made up the sabban were Binut Drudach, Masta Drudach, and the Tiqadh Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Desert's Gifthouse The guildhall of the Guild of Glassblowers and Bottle-Makers. It was well known for the  tall hourglass attached to its minaret, which would through magic periodically flip itself every four hours.Location: Binut Drudach
The Golden Maidens A festhall dating back to the 10 century DR, it was one of the most renowned sites in all of Makista Sabban. This was due to a legend that said it was once visited by avatars of Hanali Celanil, Lliira, Sharess, and Sune during its Midwinter revels.Location: Masta Drudach
Shiinalidajh The guildhall of the Glaziers' Society.Location: Tiqadh Drudach
Villa Ehmarik A luxurious residence belonging to Pasha Ehmarik.Location: Tiqadh Drudach
Vahlen Sabban
Also known as the "Meal Sabban", for the sector prided itself on its many inns and restaurants, all of which catered to the rich upper classes of Calimport society. Its banquet halls were far different from the usual Calishite dining experience, featuring extensive arrays of extravagant foods and cooking styles. This sabban was so noted for its dining experience that eating there, referred to as "Dining Vahlen", was enough to raise one's status, though only for as long as the stories of one's experience continued to garner interest among their compatriots.

Much like Makista Sabban, the buildings in this sector were quite ancient, though they were adorned in all manner of lavish decorum that so greatly enticed Calimpanni social climbers.

The sabban mark of Vahlen consisted of a small dagger, plunged into a wedge of cheese. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was scarlet red, whilst the colors of its drudachs were black, white, and yellow. The three drudachs that made up the sabban were Gimela Drudach, It'aem Drudach, and Ysaav Drudach.
Notable Locations
Cafe Cormyrean A popular inn and banquet hall that drew large crowds for its offerings of Cormyrian foods and drinks.Location: Ysaav Drudach
Guidadh's Gold An inn that was affiliated with Golden Sands Brewery.Location: It'aem Drudach
House of Hufir The private residence of the business owner Hufir el Boqariq, owner of the Cafe Cormyrean.Location: Ysaav Drudach
The Samehlariq A tall wizard's tower.Location: Gimela Drudach

## Calimport/Jewel Ward

Jewel Ward was an upper-class district of Calimport and was one of the city's seven Central Wards. It stood out as the predominant home of Calimport's gemcutters and whitesmiths, though this inherent labor-focused aspect of the ward made it considered less prestigious by the "noble" denizens of the neighboring Grand and Palace Wards.

Location
This area was located in the western center of the city, sandwiched between Grand Ward to the east and Palace Ward to the west. To the north it was bordered by the Faiths and Trades Wards. And to the south it bordered the Dock Ward.

History
The area was formerly part of separate city quarters, before Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal established the system of wards in the, superseding the long-standing system of sabbans and drudachs. Leading up to this point, over the course of a few centuries the areas that would be delineated as the Grand, Jewel, and Palace wards underwent vertical construction by the Circle of Architects, Engineers, and Builders. This was done with the intention of providing both the upper classes and their servants greater areas of mobility, as well as to keep the latter out of sight.

Government
In the late 14th century DR, the Sultan of Jewel Ward was Janar yn Janar el Vyrsaty. And as one of the high priests of the Temple of Old Night, he had a myriad of influence in the Muzhahajaarnadah, which he leveraged to pit certain elements against one another for his own personal gain.

Trade
Over 60% of Calimport's black-market trade in weapons and magic goods was conducted on the understreets of Jewel Ward. The lower levels of legitimate businesses were also known to deal in the same goods that they peddled on the upperstreets of Jewel Ward, just with far less reservation about who they sold to. Shops that did business on the lower level also had less reservations about what wares they sold, how they disguised their wares, or even how they altered them.

Inhabitants
The lower level of the ward, out of sight of the upper classes, was reserved for their servants and slaves. Life here largely operated as any other part of Calimport, but due to its obscured nature many sultans, pashas, and the like conducted clandestine activities there with the city's criminal powers.

Sabbans
Jewel Ward was divided into three sabbans and nine drudachs. However, much like its neighbors, the distinctions between these sabbans and drudachs was blurred due to its layered infrastructure.

The slightly vaulted, stonework secondary layer of Jewel Ward was the "ground level" to its rich denizens. Braced by both stone and timber supports, it was comprised of solid street avenues and courts, granting the upper classes more uninterrupted movement than the sabban-wall byways afforded. The engineers responsible constructed it in such a manner as to ensure that it would stay elevated even if half of these timber supports were broken. One could access the city's true ground level and vice-versa by traversing sets of stairs.

The edges of the ward's byways, the primary "roads" upon which moneyed folk traveled across the lengths of Calimport, served as the "curbs" of this layer. As the boundary defining sabban marks were not present on the second layer, those that walked its elevated streets used the glazed coloration of these curbs to determine which sabban and drudach they were standing in. Each were assigned a distinct coloration, with the latter being denoted as a stripe at the base of the sabban color.

The lower level of Jewel Ward was often lumped together with those of the Grand and Palace wards as the "Upper Muzad", being considered the uppermost layer of the Muzhahajaarnadah. In some areas there were even said to be hidden entrances to the Muzad. With the sky blocked out by the elevated streets, save for stairwells and the gates to the open-air Outer or Port Wards, torches had to be relied upon for illumination.
Kalil's Sabban
Kalil's Sabban was the foremost sector of inscribing and fine detailing, home to artists that created quite ornate hilts and weapons. It was also considered the place to go if one desired concealed weaponry, hidden with jewelry or other such items.

The sabban's name was considered somewhat atypical of sabban naming conventions. Both it and its many aliases—Butcher's Sabban, Sholehfall Sabban, and Vihad Sabban—were all derived from Kalil Vihad, a brutal warrior pasha during the Forth Age of Calimshan who destroyed the Sholeh Dynasty.

Reflecting the brutal origins of its name, the mark of Kalil's Sabban was a pair of scimitars, crossed beneath a skull. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was a deep purple, whilst the colors at their base representing its drudachs were black, gray, and white.It is not specified anywhere within the text which color each drudach is associated with. The three drudachs that made up the sabban were Ehraam Drudach, Solem Drudach, and Yuzhad Drudach.
Notable Locations
Butrys Villa The luxurious residence of Butrys el Alix, the sabbalad of Kalil's Sabban.Location: Solem Drudach
House of Salim el Khufu The private residence of Salim el Khufu, the druzir of Ehraam Drudach.Location: Ehraam Drudach
The Tycharradah An ancient Beshaban temple that had formerly been dedicated to the goddess Tyche.Location: Ehraam Drudach
The Gilded Lantern The guildhall of the Shining Order of Goldsmiths and Gilders.Location: Yuzhad Drudach
Mjôm Sabban
Also known as the "The Marriage Sabban", due in part to its predominant industries of silk importation and jewelry crafting and selling.

The other inspiration for the name was a particularly gruesome murder of a bridal procession that occurred in -187 DR. Whilst en-route to the House of the Holy Dawn, the procession was murdered by the groom's political rivals. Since that day, the victims' ghosts would manifest in the understreets of Mjôm Sabban upon the anniversary of their murder. Their bodies would begin as white and insubstantial in form, shifting into a red shade the closer they got to the side of their murder, until finally fading away with mournful wails as they got within  of the temple.

The sabban mark of Mjôm consisted of two linked rings, set upon a diamond field. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was blaze orange, whilst the colors at their base representing its drudachs were russet red, slate gray, and sunflower yellow. The three drudachs that made up the sabban were Akklah Drudach, Ginayna Drudach, and Kadaladh Drudach.
Notable Locations
Abhuk Villa The private residence of Asraf el Abhuk, a minor pasha and the druzir of Kadaladh Drudach in the 14 century DR. It was most notable for a khamarkha in its rear grounds, which concealed within a Waukeenar shrine a two-way portal to the Lost Level of Undermountain.Location: Kadaladh Drudach
Aratabarh The guildhall of the Lock and Finesmiths' Guild.Location: Ginayna Drudach
House of the Holy Dawn A temple dedicated to Lathander.Location: Akklah Drudach

Nadana Sabban
Also known as the "Gem Sabban", for this sector of the ward was the predominant home of gemcutters and the city's gem trade. Being that such a high value commodity was dealt with in this sabban, it had a far higher presence of amlakkar and mercenary guards than anywhere else in the city, save for the Pasha's Sabban. Over half of its residents were guards, with the interests in either certain guilds or families. And what few khanduqs were present were all magically protected, ensuring both raw and finished gems were safely stored.

The sabban mark of Nadana was a gem cut in crown fashion, with seven facets. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was white, whilst the colors at their base representing its drudachs were emerald green, royal blue, and royal purple. The three drudachs that made up the sabban were Octel Drudach,  Parlial Drudach, and Tiagar Drudach.
Notable Locations
Four Bezels The luxurious guildhall of the Society of Diligent Gemcutters.Location: Parlial Drudach
Khafif Villa The large, luxurious private residence of Pasha Khafif.Location: Octel Drudach
Lupalidah The towering guildhall of the Jewellers' Guild.Location: Tiagar Drudach
Vyrsatyr VillaThe large, luxurious private residence of Vyrsatyr.Location: Octel Drudach
Yisaemid Villa The luxury residence of Yisaemid, the sabbalad of Nadana and the druzir of Tiagar in the 14 century DR.Location: Tiagar Drudach

## Castle of glass

The castle of glass was the name by which tales among the Ffolk of the Moonshae Isles identified a legendary and hidden location atop Highpeak in the Orcskull Mountains of Moray. Although largely a topic of tall tales, the castle did indeed exist.

Location
The castle's exact location was unknown. According to the tales, the glass structure was said to be all but impossible to see by mortals. It lay high in the Orcskulls surrounded by impassable chasms filled with jagged rocks at the bottom. The castle proper was said to be surrounded by magical trees, the fruit of which could ward off disease and even death.

Structure
The castle could only be reached by a long, slender, and equally invisible drawbridge. Both the castle and the bridge said to be beautiful, delicate, and made all of glass.

Rumors & Legends

According to an old Moonshae tale, a woman known as the maiden of Highpeak and her sons dwelt in this grand glass castle atop the mountain. The sons grew tired of living in the castle, and so they constructed a glass bridge to a nearby mountain, and set out to explore. However, as they left, the castle disappeared. All but the oldest son would go on to die in battle, at which point he returned home and managed to rediscover the bridge during a bitter winter. As he crossed it, he slipped on the ice and fell to his death. The woman was grief-stricken, and her cries could henceforth be heard echoing out of the mountains during hot summers or freezing winters. The tale concluded with the thought that, one day, a descendant of the maiden would rediscover the castle and relieve the mother's suffering.

## Calimport/Palace Ward

Palace Ward was the foremost upper-class district of Calimport, the richest of all wards, and was one of the city's seven Central Wards.

Location
This area was located in the western center of the city, sandwiched between Jewel Ward to the east and Shackles Ward to the west. More specifically, it abutted Qhibal Sabban, the most prosperous and clean sector of Shackles Ward. To the north it was bordered by the Faiths Ward. And to the south it bordered the Armada and Dock Wards. At the very heart of Palace Ward stood the Pasha's Sabban, an area that held the unique distinction of being considered its own jurisdiction on par with a ward.

History
The area was formerly part of the Temple and Learning Quarter, before Syl-Pasha Ralan el Pesarkhal established the system of wards in the, superseding the long-standing system of sabbans and drudachs. Leading up to this point, over the course of a few centuries the areas that would be delineated as the Grand, Jewel, and Palace wards underwent vertical construction by the Circle of Architects, Engineers, and Builders. This was done with the intention of providing both the upper classes and their servants greater areas of mobility, as well as to keep the latter out of sight.

In 1092 DR, Palace Ward's Darehj Sabban was one of many affected by the blaze later known as Akham's Duel.

In the, the Syl-Pasha broke ground on a long-term construction project, a defensive barrier he dubbed the Pesarkhal Wall. By the next year it encompassed the Armada, Palace, and Shackles Wards. El Pesarkhal planned for it to eventually enclose the entirety of the Central Wards.

Government
In the late 14th century DR, the Sultan of Palace Ward was Tomuk yn Jhiavor el Kahmir. Though he was a daft, ineffectual, and paranoid sultan he managed to maintain his position on account of being the second grandson of Nur el Kahmir, the Pasha of Manshaka, another city in Calimshan that was allied to El Pesarkhal.

Inhabitants
The upper streets of Palace Ward were home to some of the most affluent and richest people in Calimshan, as well as a great deal of the pashas, the leaders of the city's guilds and businesses. Many of these residents were of the "old money" variety, being inheritors of their considerable wealth.

The lower level of the ward, out of sight of the upper classes, was reserved for their servants and slaves. Life here largely operated as any other part of Calimport, but due to its obscured nature many sultans, pashas, and the like conducted clandestine activities in the understreets with the city's criminal powers.

Sabbans
Palace Ward was largely a residential ward, with much of its space occupied by the villas of pashas, often only being broken up by the likes of row houses, taverns, and the garrisons for hired guards and mercenaries. The area was divided into three sabbans and ten drudachs. However, much like its neighbors, the distinctions between these sabbans and drudachs was blurred due to its layered infrastructure.

The slightly vaulted, stonework secondary layer of Palace Ward was the "ground level" to its rich denizens. Braced by both stone and timber supports, it was comprised of solid street avenues and courts, granting the upper classes more uninterrupted movement than the sabban-wall byways afforded. The engineers responsible constructed it in such a manner as to ensure that it would stay elevated even if half of these timber supports were broken. One could access the city's true ground level and vice-versa by traversing sets of stairs.

The edges of the ward's byways, the primary "roads" upon which moneyed folk traveled across the lengths of Calimport, served as the "curbs" of this layer. As the boundary defining sabban marks were not present on the second layer, those that walked its elevated streets used the glazed coloration of these curbs to determine which sabban and drudach they were standing in. Each were assigned a distinct coloration, with the latter being denoted as a stripe at the base of the sabban color.

The lower level of Palace Ward was often lumped together with those of the Grand and Jewel wards as the "Upper Muzad", being considered the uppermost layer of the Muzhahajaarnadah. In some areas there were even said to be hidden entrances to the Muzad. With the sky blocked out by the elevated streets, save for stairwells and the gates to the open-air Outer or Port Wards, torches had to be relied upon for illumination.
Darehj Sabban
Also known as the "Mosaic Sabban", due to the myriad of inlaid mosaics that adorned its upraised street sections and many buildings. It was one of two sabbans in Palace Ward that lied along the Pesarkhal Wall. And as it abutted the Armada and Shackles Wards, its business and residents were heavily involved in the sea and slave trades.

The sabban mark of Darehj depicted a straight line of five chain links. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was scarlet red, whilst the colors at their base representing its drudachs were black, white, and yellow.It is not specified anywhere within the text which color each drudach is associated with. The three drudachs that made up the sabban were Adhaef Drudach, Borto Drudach, and Dehk Drudach.
Notable Locations
Hidashar Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Hidashar.Location: Dehk Drudach
House of the Veil Gizara The guildhall of the Aromatic Order of Perfumists, Apothecarists, and Soap-Makers.Location: Dehk Drudach
Iserib Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Iserib.Location: Adhaef Drudach
The Plaza of Divine Truth A fortified temple complex dedicated to Bhaelros. It was among the largest of Calimport's temples and sported nearly a dozen small shrines in addition to its central major temple.Location: Borto Drudach
Square of the Djen An open courtyard decorated in free-form mosaic patterns. It was both an assembly ground and a common meeting place for Calimpanni from all professions and social classes. It was notably one of the few, if not only, areas in Calimport where blood had never been spilled. An intense superstition surrounded breaking the sanctity of this, to the point that any who attempted to do so would be dragged out and torn apart by a fearful mob.Location: Borto Drudach
Synnabat Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Synnabat.Location: Adhaef Drudach

Khatrev Sabban
Also known as the "Jhambiya Sabban", a disparaging nickname born from a long reputation as a site of assassinations. This northernmost sector offered the easiest ingress to the Pasha's Sabban.

It was one of the two sabbans in Palace Ward that bordered the Pesarkhal Wall. The gatehouses between that outer wall and Khatrev Sabban's own inner walls were not heavily guarded, for most guards were instead stationed at the area of highest traffic, the sabban's conenction to Faiths Ward.

The sabban mark of Khatrev was a crude depiction of a jambiya, consisting of a curled slash with a perpendicular slash across its upper end. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was black, whilst the colors at their base representing its drudachs were green, sky blue, and turquoise. The three drudachs that made up the sabban were Nar'asr Drudach, Qadeem Drudach, and Sra'ala Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Circle's Ovens The guildhall of the Most Skilled Circle of Cooks and Tasters.Location: Sra'ala Drudach
Haesib Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Haesib.Location: Nar'asr Drudach
Kahmir Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Kahmir.Location: Qadeem Drudach
The Quiver The guildhall of the Council of Bowyers and Fletchers.Location: Qadeem Drudach
The Silkhanduq The guildhall of the Jhasinnar Sodality.Location: Nar'asr Drudach
Talaeta Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Talaeta.Location: Sra'ala Drudach
Najlet Sabban
Also known by the monikers "Demonshadow Sabban" and "The Martyr's Sabban", in remembrance of a significant event that occurred in the sabban back during the Eighth Age of Calimshan. In the, a rival for the throne conjured a rogue tanar'ri by the name of Chanaavokh. It rampaged across the streets of Calimport, killing all who crossed its path, until over 200 laid slain.

The then-Syl Pasha's second son, Ikham yn Herak el Najle, confronted the vile fiend amid a ruined courtyard and the rubble of two buildings. He fought Chanaavokh to a stand still, their battle eventually ending in their mutual demise. As their blood intermingled, the stone upon which they fell was stained dark red. Ever since that day, a dark silhouette of the two was present, and when upperstreets were constructed a dark outline appeared on the stone street directly overhead of the original site.

Najlet Sabban's mark reflected this story and the strange stain it left behind on the sabban, consisting of a silhouetted head with greatly exaggerated horns on its sides. The color displayed on the edges of its walls was royal blue, whilst the colors at their base representing its drudachs were golden rod yellow, ivory, and kelly green.Despite having four separate drudachs, the text only lists three drudach colors for Najlet Sabban. The four drudachs that made up the sabban were Calimra Drudach, Ilhif Drudach, Tistad Drudach, and Vina'atf Drudach.
Notable Locations
Cemberyl Stables A stables business.Location: Ilhif Drudach
The Globe Well An incredibly ancient well, located at the central hub of Najlet Sabban, that reached down into a subterranean source of water. It was enchanted by a bakkal court vizar back during the First Age of Calimshan, given a magical effect that would make it periodically draw water up from below.Location: Ilhif Drudach
Haraf Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Haraf.Location: Tistad Drudach
Haris Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Haris.Location: Calimra Drudach
Keffiyehdah The guildhall of the Most Splendid Order of Tailors.Location: Calimra Drudach
Mitayn Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Mitayn.Location: Vina'atf Drudach
Witmaanal's Livery A business that offered stabling.Location: Ilhif Drudach
Yshriin Villa The luxurious residence of Pasha Yshriin.Location: Ilhif Drudach
Ytal's Confectioners A confectionery shop on the ground floor of a row house.Location: Tistad Drudach

## Caleph's Gate

Caleph's Gate was a barbican gate that guarded passage into the Pasha's Sabban, the seat of power in the city of Calimport. Though there were some secret entrances into the sabban, as far as the vast majority of Calimpanni knew, it was the only entrance.

Structure
This fortified structure stood two stories tall, or roughly . It had a set of three portcullises built into it, which could be dropped down at any time to deter unwanted entry. And both atop and aside the entryway were a number of murder holes for the defenders to shoot through.

As a last line of defense against unwavering resistance, gates had a trapdoor floor. By drawing away the supports below, the hinged floor inside could be opened up by, unveiling a  drop into a pit lined with stakes.

Defenses
At any given time there were eight guards stationed at the Caleph's Gate. Four were posted atop it, two outside of it, and two just inside its walls.

## Calimport/Maker's Ward

Maker's Ward was a ward of Calimport dominated by skilled tradesmen and trade guilds. It was also one of the city's seven Central Wards.

Location
This area was located in the eastern center of the city, sandwiched between Wizard Ward to the west, a bit of Quill Ward's Jhaapir Sabban to the northwest, and Crypt Ward to the east. To the south it was bordered by Caravans Ward and the shipyards of the Hook Ward.

Government
In the 14th century DR, the Sultan of Maker's Ward was Zelmazzar el Fiqr, a man who by 1370 DR was counted among the oldest government officials across all of Calimshan, due in part to his unwavering loyalty to the Caleph's Throne, rather than any one man holding the office of Syl-Pasha.

Trade
A wide variety of businesses operated in Maker's Ward, many of which benefited from the ward's close proximity to Caravans Ward. One could even find skilled craftsmen of armor and shields, though not in any particular subdivision of the area. Unlike the other major trades district, Hammer Ward, the people here were lacked any sort of altruistic communal sense of unity. Rather than working together to make the ward a better place for all, the tradesmen were fiercely competitive. Vendettas and street brawls were the norm for this area, sometimes blowing up into full scale guild wars, as guilds or families endeavored to dominate costers, particular business deals, or even specific trades.

Inhabitants
One of the remarkable aspects of Maker's Ward in the 14 century DR was its near complete lack of slaves, with all residents being free people, at least in the strictest sense of the term. Slaves were considered to be a luxury by more than half of those who inhabited the ward.

Sabbans
Maker's Ward was divided into three sabbans with nine drudachs.
Golnar Sabban
Also known as "The Builder's Sabban", for this quite dirty and noisome sabban was the home of builder tradesmen, such as carpenters and masons and the like. It was located in the southeastern section of the ward, abutting the Caravans, Crypt, and Hook Wards. Together these three wards kept the tradesmen in steady business, with fresh building materials seemingly in near-constant demand in Calimport.

The sabban mark of Golnar consisted of two tools, a hammer and a chisel, crossed over one another. The area was divided into three drudachs—Dohar Drudach, Gatab Drudach, and Rakhin Drudach.
Notable Locations
Amlakkhan Jaleh A corrupt amlakkhan that was operated by a group of thugs and extortionists. Their commanding officers controlled the protection rackets in Golnar Sabban, splitting a generous cut of the profits with the area's sabbalad. Any amlakkar who didn't cooperate with their corrupt racket would find themselves privy to "accidents" and lethal tavern brawls.Location: Rakhin Drudach
Bahil-Bakadah The guildhall of the Order of Skilled Coopers and Barrel-Makers.Location: Gatab Drudach
Sadidahjalan The guildhall of the Guild of Stonecutters and Masons.Location: Dohar Drudach

Jaleh Sabban
Also known as "Saamark Sabban", was a sector of the ward predominated by sellers of rare goods, luxuries, trinkets, and amenities for assuaging inconveniences in one's life. The sundry rare goods on offer were fit for satisfying any taste one might have, whether it be antiquities or sweets. Additionally, this area was home to tradesmen of softer goods, including clothing, rugs, and tapestries.

The Jaleh Sabban's name, as well as its nickname, were derived from Saamark II el Jaleh, an overly indulgent pasha who was remembered for spending his wealth lavishly with little care for what the goods he bought actually did for him.

The sabban mark of Jaleh depicted a lion's head. The area was divided into three drudachs—Bakkrad Drudach, Lanish Drudach, and Loqha Drudach.
Notable Locations
Taerako Statuary and Stonework A business within a row house that specialized in the creation of statuary.Location: Bakkrad Drudach
Twelve Reeds House The guildhall of the Basketmakers' Guild.Location: Lanish Drudach

Sojrab Sabban
Also known as "Heart's Joy Sabban", was a sector of the ward predominated by artists. Fiercely as competive as the rest of the tradesmen of Maker's Ward, the courtyards of this sabban acted as the canvasses for impromptu sculpting competitions against one another, often times creating works solely for the purpose of outdoing their rivals. Its northeastern corner, Qanôn Drudach, was perceptively quieter than the rest due to its proximity to the Crypt and Quill Wards. Because of this, the neighborhood was a common meeting space among temperamental artists, bards, and creators of all kinds, either looking to reunite with old friends or to forge new relationships with kindred souls.

Sojrab Sabban was named in remembrance of the Sojrab Dynasty, whose pashas were largely remembered for being avid patrons of the arts and culture. The sabban's colloquial name was derived from it streets commonly being wandered through by lovers, poets, and romantics.

The sabban mark of Sojrab consisted of a harp, displayed against a triangular field, with both tapering to points at the bottom of the mark. The area was divided into three drudachs—Dowr Drudach, Qanôn Drudach, and Tar'ea Drudach.
Notable Locations
The Brothers Humuz A business within a row house that was owned by two brothers. It specialized in the production of interior murals for mud brick and stone walls.Location: Tar'ea Drudach
Casters' Claim The guildhall of the Pewterers' and Casters' Guild.Location: Dowr Drudach
Salehlon's Carpets A business within a row house that specialized in the creation of mundane and magic carpets.Location: Qanôn Drudach

History
In the, Maker's Ward's Golnar Sabban was one of many affected by the blaze later known as Akham's Duel.

In 1370 DR, some of the city's newest khanduqs could be found in Maker's Ward.
